articles.title: ‘Unusually large’ multi-state storm causing severe weather for Australia’s east – with more on the way
articles.summary: BoM predicts hail, damaging winds, flash flooding and power outages across southern Queensland, western NSW, the ACT and eastern Victoria on Sunday afternoon Get our breaking news email , free app or…
articles.byline: Graham Readfearn Environment and climate correspondent

blocks.text: Large parts of eastern Australia were put on alert for severe thunderstorms on Sunday afternoon with more potential storms and flood risk in store for Monday.

The Bureau of Meteorology said a broad line of storms had already swept through western New South Wales, while eight flood warnings were in place across southern Queensland after days of torrential rain.

Severe thunderstorms that could bring hail, damaging winds, flash flooding and power outages were likely over a huge area on Sunday afternoon, the bureau said, including across southern Queensland, western NSW, the ACT and eastern Victoria.
Wind gusts of up to 100km/h were recorded in the central west of NSW around midday on Sunday with the bureau warning residents of further likely thunderstorm warnings to come on Sunday evening.
“This is a multi-state system of storms and it’s unusually large,” said bureau meteorologist David Crock.
Crock said an area of high pressure had been sitting over the Tasman Sea for the past 10 days that had been blocking weather fronts and bringing storms and rains to southern Queensland.
“Eventually you get a strong enough system that pushes that blocking pattern away and that typically brings severe weather with it,” he said.

blocks.caption: A car engulfed by flood waters on Buchanan Road at Morayfield, north of Brisbane on 22 October. Photograph: Darren England/AAP

blocks.text: A front of cooler air was moving from the west on Sunday afternoon, dragging in tropical moisture from the north and bringing storm conditions to central parts of NSW and to Canberra on Sunday afternoon.

“We have a big line of storms that’s extending all the way from the Snowy mountains to the Queensland border. Behind that we are watching to see if there’s going to another band developing behind it.”
Storm activity was likely to continue through Sunday evening and into Monday in northern NSW and southern Queensland as the cold front continued to push.
“[Monday] is the last big bang of this system and that’s going to be a great relief for those people in south-east Queensland,” he said.
after newsletter promotion
Southern parts of Queensland had been through a weather “whiplash” in the past week, Crock said.
Some eight flood warnings were in place over southern Queensland. The Mary River downstream of Gympie was forecast to reach major flood levels in Tiaro on Sunday evening and into Monday.

After a very dry September, southern parts of the state had seen October rainfall “multiple times their average” for the month, Crock said, with areas around the Sunshine Coast seeing between 200mm and 400mm of rain in the past week.
The bureau’s current long-range forecast for November to January suggests rainfall is likely to be above average over most of the country except the far north and much of Tasmania.
November is likely to be warmer than usual for the southern half of the continent, with night-time temperatures in particular forecast to be likely well above average over most of the country.
Global heating has seen Australia warm by about 1.5C since 1910, the bureau’s long-term climate data shows.

articles.title: Israel to close West Bank crossings on election day as crackdown escalates
articles.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces announces restrictions on the movement of Palestinian workers in the run-up to Tuesday's election.

blocks.text: All West Bank land crossings will be closed during Tuesday's election in Israel, the country's military says, and Palestinian workers will be barred from entering all settlements.
The restrictions come amid a crackdown in the occupied West Bank after Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers in the territory.

The Israel Defense Forces announced a "ban on the entry and exit of Palestinian workers throughout Judea and Samaria and the Jordan Valley, including industrial zones, as well as the closure of all land crossings" on Tuesday.
It said most workers would also be barred from settlements from Sunday, with the exception of industrial zones and a limited number of other areas.
Before the Hamas-led October 7, 2023 attack on Israel, more than 100,000 Palestinian workers were permitted to enter Israel. Since then only a small fraction have had their permits restored.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced a major operation on Friday in response to the killing of two Israeli soldiers by two Palestinian gunmen in an attack on a checkpoint. Three other Israeli soldiers were injured, and the gunmen were also killed.
The Israeli military have been demolishing homes and businesses in the city of Hebron, with hundreds of families having been displaced.

Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said about 2,000 residents had been displaced by the operation, which has led to at least one whole street appearing to have been flattened, according to footage shared online.
Even before the entry and exit bans on workers were announced by the IDF on Sunday, the military had cordoned off the city, heavily restricting the movement of its 200,000 residents.

It is common for Israeli forces to demolish the homes of Palestinians who are suspected of carrying out attacks on Israelis in the West Bank - a practice Israeli rights groups have criticised as collective punishment.
Friday's shooting came during a tense time for the region, just days ahead of Israel's election taking place on Tuesday.
In an interview with Israel's i24 television channel released on Saturday, Netanyahu threatened a "very big surprise" for the Palestinian Authority (PA), which governs parts of the territory.
Hebron Mayor Youssef al-Jaabari said the operation was being "driven by the elections" and that Netanyahu and his ministers were attempting to secure the votes of the far right and the settlers.
On Saturday, thousands gathered in Tel Aviv for a large anti-government demonstration.

The protest was organised by the October Council, a group founded by the families of victims and hostages taken by militants on 7 October 2023, to demand accountability for the failure to prevent the Hamas-led attack.

"Three days before the election, we will hold the culminating event marking three years of struggle to uncover the truth, demand accountability, and establish a state commission of inquiry," the October Council wrote on X ahead of the rally.
The gathering saw the participation of the leaders of the four main opposition parties, including Gadi Eisenkot, the former military chief of staff who is neck and neck with Netanyahu.

articles.title: Before the Philippines even had a name, it had gold
articles.summary: “When you look at this gold jewelry, you realize that once upon a time we had a golden age. It gives you a sense of what was pre-colonial culture,” historian Ambeth Ocampo tells Rappler

blocks.text: “When you look at this gold jewelry, you realize that once upon a time we had a golden age. It gives you a sense of what was pre-colonial culture,” historian Ambeth Ocampo tells Rappler

items: Gold, a durable and timeless metal, has been crafted into intricate ornaments by ancient Filipinos long before colonial times, showcasing a rich cultural heritage.

The accidental discovery of ancient gold artifacts in 1981 by Edilberto Morales led to the recovery of significant treasures, which were later preserved in collections at the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas and Ayala Museum.

The gold artifacts reveal advanced craftsmanship and social stratification in pre-colonial Philippine society, challenging conventional historical narratives and highlighting a 'golden age' of cultural pride.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Gold is a patient metal. It does not rust or decay. It can be melted, worn, used, and reused from one generation to another, surviving long after the hands that first fashioned it have turned to dust.

And more than a thousand years ago, long before these islands were called the Philippines, our ancestors were already working gold into exquisite ornaments, delicate chains, and elaborate vessels. Some of these treasures have survived to the present day; in them, we see a glimpse of a civilization nearly forgotten.
Their rediscovery was a golden accident.
On a sunny April day in 1981, Edilberto “Mang Berto” Morales was operating heavy machinery for a government irrigation project in Surigao del Sur. Something glistened in the mud.
What he mistook for a helmet turned out to be a partly crushed gold bowl. Suspecting more, he shooed away his coworker and searched alone, combing some 300 feet of earth until late afternoon.

By day’s end, he had recovered around 22 pounds of ancient gold, including an extraordinary necklace he called kuwintas ni nanay (mother’s necklace.) He hid the long chain around his waist, beneath his shirt, away from curious eyes.
Now in the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) collection, it consists of 12 individual kamagi necklaces joined end to end, their intricate links resembling one woven cord.

blocks.caption: Photo from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas

blocks.text: But the treasure began to scatter almost as soon as it emerged. Treasure hunters recovered more gold, dispersing objects among collectors and separating pieces of the same ornament.
Then-central bank governor Jaime Laya and collectors Leandro and Cecilia Locsin helped preserve significant portions, which entered the collections of the BSP and Ayala Museum.

blocks.caption: ‘Holy grail’: Juan Luna’s lost masterpiece revealed after 132 years

blocks.text: Florina Capistrano-Baker, the scholar behind the newly launched book Bahandi, calls the two collections as “twins separated at birth.”
“They preserve different parts of a shared history and even different parts of what was once one object,” she said on Thursday, October 22, during the book’s launch at the BSP.
In 2024, selected pieces were reunited at Ayala Museum, where the exhibition is scheduled to run until 2027.

And what a magnificent history they reveal. Ancient goldsmiths mastered techniques involving minute golden beads, delicate filigree, and interlocking chains so precise that the finished jewelry could resemble cloth.

“Even today, they cannot [recreate] some of it,” historian Ambeth Ocampo told Rappler in an exclusive interview, saying that ancient Filipinos possessed such a sophisticated understanding of gold that they even had distinct terms for its purity, including 24-carat and 20-carat gold.

Gold also proclaimed status. The wealthy could wear numerous chains around their necks, with some ornaments so heavy that their wearers were said to stoop beneath their weight, BSP Deputy Governor Bernadette Romulo-Puyat recounted in a separate interview with Rappler.
Yet these were more than displays of extravagance.

blocks.caption: PAST. Florina Capistrano-Baker tells the crowd about the treasures that help us understand what a pre-colonial Philippines was like. Photo by Lance Spencer Yu/Rappler

blocks.text: “These are not just splendid ornaments. They’re evidence of social stratification, craft specialization, technical knowledge, and affluent individuals who had the means to commission these luxury goods,” Capistrano-Baker explained.

The treasure also points toward ancient Butuan, whose communities traded across the seas long before Spanish colonization. Their surviving goldwork bears influences shared with Java and other parts of South and Southeast Asia, suggesting a world of exchange far richer than conventional colonial histories might suggest.
For Ocampo, the gold offers a rich rebuttal for Filipinos raised on histories that often begin with the arrival of foreigners.
“When you look at this gold jewelry, you realize that once upon a time we had a golden age,” he told Rappler. “So it gives you a sense of pride, gives you a sense of what was pre-colonial culture.”
At the launch of Bahandi, BSP Governor Eli Remolona likened the generations who made, discovered, and preserved the treasure to links in a kamagi.
“May future generations find their place in the chain and ensure it never breaks,” he said. – Rappler.com

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump on Saturday announced that German car producer, Audi, will build a $4 billion (€3.77 billion) assembly plant in the US state of Georgia.
Speaking at a campaign rally in Perry, Georgia, Trump said the plant will produce 200,000 SUVs annually.
"Think of that. 200,000 cars a year. That's incredible," Trump said.
The US president credited his tariff policies for the company's decision to build the plant in the US.
Europe tries to sway Trump on vehicle tariffs
Trump focusing on manufacturing as midterms loom
The US leader has pressured foreign and domestic businesses to move production to the United States. His tactics included sweeping tariffs on car imports.
Last year, Trump's tariffs cost Audi €1.2-billion-euro ($1.4-billion).

The latest announcement comes as Trump tries to make a last ditch effort to boost Republican candidates in the battleground state by following through on his promise of reinvigorate American manufacturing ahead of the midterm elections.
The Republicans are bracing for losses in the November 3 vote amid rising prices and the ongoing war in Iran.
What did Audi say?
Audi, which is owned by Volkswagen, said the construction of the manufacturing plant is ‌scheduled ​to begin next year, with car production starting in the early 2030s.
How will US tariffs hit Germany's car exports and imports?

articles.title: Obama unloads on Trump while stumping for Democrats ahead of midterms
articles.summary: Obama frames the November 3 vote as a 'circuit breaker' to 'at least rein in some of the foolishness' of Trump's presidency

blocks.text: OBAMA. Former US President Barack Obama campaigns for Democratic US Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed and Democratic gubernatorial candidate Jocelyn Benson at a rally in Detroit, Michigan, US October 24, 2026.
Rebecca Cook/REUTERS
Obama frames the November 3 vote as a 'circuit breaker' to 'at least rein in some of the foolishness' of Trump's presidency

items: Barack Obama campaigned for Democratic candidates, framing the upcoming midterm elections as a chance to rein in Trump's presidency and calling for accountability in government.
Obama criticized Trump for corruption and ineptitude, highlighting public concerns about the President's financial dealings and foreign policy, particularly regarding Iran.
The former president's appearances aimed to energize Democratic voters in tight races, using humor and sharp critiques to draw contrasts with the Trump administration.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
US President Donald Trump has been telling voters to view the midterm elections as if he were on the ballot, and on Saturday, October 14, one of his Democratic predecessors did just that.

Ten days out from the elections that will determine control of the closely divided Congress, Barack Obama took to the campaign trail to accuse the Republican president of corruption, deride his strategy for Iran, and skewer the gilded aesthetic he has applied to White House renovations.

Obama stumped for Democratic candidates at rallies in Cleveland and Detroit, lampooning the Trump administration. Campaigning in Michigan for US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, Obama framed the November 3 vote as a “circuit breaker” to “at least rein in some of the foolishness” of Trump’s presidency.
“We got to flip that circuit breaker, bring some accountability to this government,” Obama said.

Obama, president from 2009 until Trump began his first term in 2017, remains one of the most popular figures among Democrats. They hope that bringing him into the race can fire up their supporters for a tight US Senate race in which El-Sayed faces Republican Mike Rogers, a former US representative.
The former president obliged the Michigan crowd by playing to Democrats’ frequently repeated criticisms of Trump and of Republicans’ willingness to go along with him.

“We have never seen a president excel in straight-up grifting, on your dime, like this,” Obama said. “Never seen a president so intent on selling favors like this…. Now the party seems to stand for corrupt government, or inept government, or no government.”

blocks.caption: Three issues defining the 2026 US midterm elections

blocks.text: The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

A Reuters/Ipsos poll in August found that 63% of Americans think the president and his family have inappropriately profited from cryptocurrency since he returned to the White House last year and that 69% believe his policy decisions are influenced by his private business dealings.

Obama also ridiculed the administration’s claims of victory against Iran. He argued that the war has given Iran more economic leverage because its threats to attack shipping in the Strait of Hormuz have unsettled oil exporters.
“Iran now has veto power over the Strait of Hormuz, where oil goes through to get to the world,” Obama said.

The former president also accused the Trump administration of emphasizing unimportant matters, sarcastically calling Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth someone “laser-focused on important matters like the jawline and testosterone levels of our troops” and ridiculing White House renovations as tacky.
“He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory,” Obama said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: How Manny Pacquiao impacted UFC’s Aaron Pico
articles.summary: ‘His fights were never boring,’ says mixed martial artist Aaron Pico of Manny Pacquiao. ‘That’s what I’m trying to do, too, here in the UFC.’

blocks.text: DOMINANT. American MMA fighter Aaron Pico celebrates winning over Guinea’s Losene Keita in UFC.
UFC
‘His fights were never boring,’ says mixed martial artist Aaron Pico of Manny Pacquiao. ‘That’s what I’m trying to do, too, here in the UFC.’

items: Manny Pacquiao's influence extends beyond boxing, impacting athletes like UFC fighter Aaron Pico, who trained at Wild Card Boxing Club and had a chance to spar with Pacquiao but missed the opportunity due to a scheduling conflict.

Pico reflects on the missed chance to learn from Pacquiao, describing him as a living legend whose intensity and passion made him an exciting fighter, and he wishes he had taken the opportunity to spar with him.
Despite not sparring with Pacquiao, Pico cherishes memories of watching Pacquiao's fights with family and aims to bring the same excitement to his own fights in the UFC.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Manny Pacquiao’s influence stretches far beyond boxing, reaching athletes across combat sports.
Among them is UFC featherweight Aaron Pico, who once came close to sharing the ring with the Filipino boxing legend.
Pico, known for his elite freestyle wrestling, trained with Pacquiao’s longtime coach Freddie Roach at the renowned Wild Card Boxing Club in California, where he sharpened his striking skills.
In 2017, the highly touted American prospect even had a chance to travel to the Philippines and serve as Pacquiao’s sparring partner ahead of his bout against Australian boxer Jeff Horn.
But the plan fell through because Pico had a professional fight scheduled around the same time.
“The first time I sparred at Wild Card, or during one of the few times I sparred there, Freddie was watching,” Pico told Rappler.

“When he was preparing for the fight against Jeff Horn, Freddie asked me, ‘Do you want to go to the Philippines and be a sparring partner for Manny? I think you’d be a good look for Manny in preparation for Jeff Horn.’”
Looking back, Pico wishes he had taken the opportunity to work with Pacquiao, who went on to lose to Horn by controversial unanimous decision in Brisbane.

The chance would have been about more than just a sparring session for Pico. For him, it would have meant learning from a living legend whose intensity and passion made him one of the most exciting fighters of his generation.
“Looking back, I probably would have just said, ‘Hey, I’ll go and spar Manny,’ because he’s a living legend. It would have been a great experience for me,” Pico said.
“His intensity was something I could really pick up. It’s just unfortunate it did not happen, but I got a taste of that passion from Freddie.”

Pico returned to the UFC spotlight on Sunday, October 25 (Manila time), needing just over a minute to TKO Guinea’s Losene Keita in their featherweight fight, an event made available in the Philippines via ESPN on Disney+.
Pico improved his MMA record to 15-5, winning back-to-back fights. Keita, who previously split his last four, slipped to 17-3.
The 30-year-old American was originally scheduled to fight Arnold Allen, who withdrew because of an injury, paving the way for Keita to step in on short notice.
Even without getting the chance to spar with Pacquiao, Pico has carried fond memories of watching the Filipino icon fight.

Growing up in California, Pico experienced the same fight-night tradition familiar to many Filipino families. Whenever Pacquiao competed, relatives and friends gathered to watch, turning his bouts into major occasions.
As Pacquiao took on some of the best Mexican and American fighters of his era, his relentless pace and explosive style captivated a young Pico.

“He didn’t really influence my fighting style, but as a fan, I enjoyed watching him,” Pico said. “Whenever Manny fought, my family would get together for big barbecues, and everyone would get really excited, especially me.”
“He was such an exciting fighter to watch.”
As Pico looks to establish himself among the UFC’s top featherweights, he hopes to deliver the same kind of excitement that made Pacquiao a global attraction.
He knows the sports are different, but the goal remains the same: give fans a fight worth watching.

“His fights were never boring. You knew that when you paid for the pay-per-view, you were going to get your money’s worth,” Pico said. “That’s what I’m trying to do, too, here in the UFC.” – with a report from Drew Lo/Rappler.com

articles.title: AFP boss says politicians’ heated rhetoric is fuelling threats against MPs
articles.summary: Commissioner Krissy Barrett says women are more often singled out, often with threats of sexual violence Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australia’s top federal law…

blocks.text: Australia’s top federal law enforcement official has drawn a direct link between politicians’ rhetoric and threats and abuse being directed at leaders.
The safety of elected representatives at all levels has been thrown into the spotlight after independent MP Helen Haines was allegedly deliberate attacked outside her Wangaratta electoral office.
Haines remains in a serious but stable condition at the Alfred hospital in Melbourne, following her double leg amputation.
The Australian federal police commissioner, Krissy Barrett, said there was no doubt the threat environment had changed for politicians.

“When I start work every morning, one of the first things I do is read a report … [that] summarises all of the threats that have been reported to the AFP over the last 24 hours,” she told the ABC’s Insiders program.
“Now, some days that report is pages and pages long.”
The commissioner said she wasn’t interested in policing free speech or intervening in political discourse.

“But I would challenge any Australian to read some of these threats and some of the abuse that is reported to us from federal parliamentarians and for anyone to argue that that is free speech or political discourse,” she added.

The move from the sending of physical hate mail to online threats had played a significant role in the increasing volume of worrying material, while also highlighting the influence of inflammatory political imagery and language.

“We do see where there is particular political conflict or discourse occurring … it does have a direct correlation to what we see in terms of threats and abuse, and sometimes it’s very immediate,” Barrett said.
Past One Nation cartoons depicting political figures, including the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, being hit by cars or buses have resurfaced in the days since the alleged attack on Haines.
The AFP commissioner said there was “a reaction amongst the community” to material such as the cartoons.

blocks.caption: Tributes outside the Wangaratta electoral office of independent federal MP Helen Haines on 20 October.  Photograph: James Ross/EPA

blocks.text: The policing agency, which is responsible for protecting federal politicians and office-holders, has held a number of emergency safety briefings with parliamentarians since Monday.
after newsletter promotion
Male and female MPs were targeted equally with threats and abuse, Barrett said, but women were more often singled out individually, often with threats of sexual violence.
“My hope is that this really causes people to pause and have a think about what’s happening in this country and the impact of that,” she said.
“And if this is not the incident, then what is?”
Federal MPs from across the political spectrum have acknowledged the difficulty in balancing their personal security and access to voters.
“As a local MP, I don’t want to stop going to community events,” Liberal frontbencher Ted O’Brien told News24 on Sunday.
“That open access is a cornerstone of democracy. We’re particularly good at it in Australia. We can’t take away grassroots politics.”
Labor minister Catherine King said she has been contending with the deteriorating safety for some time.
“It is when, not if, that something will happen to one of us and we’ve been saying that certainly for the last five years or so,” she said.
“I had a mobile caravan for almost 25 years. I don’t use that now because it doesn’t have a second exit point.
“If someone did kick off and I’m trapped in the van, it’s very hard to deal with that.”

articles.title: Gunmen kill at least 10 villagers and loot shops in northeast Nigeria
articles.summary: Police are searching for other casualties, with officials warning the actual death toll could rise further.

blocks.text: Unknown gunmen have raided a remote village in the northeast Nigerian state of Taraba, killing at least 10 people, looting shops and setting houses ablaze, police say.
There are fears the actual death toll is much higher, with eyewitnesses speaking of 20 lives lost and a non-governmental organisation suggesting a toll of as many as 50.
The gunmen reportedly swooped on the village of Binnari in the Karim Lamido area mounted on motorcycles just after midday Muslim prayers on Friday in a rampage that went on for up to four hours.
Police say they are searching for other casualties in the bush but the authorities were accused by Amnesty International of failing to protect rural communities.
Nigeria continues to face attacks by armed groups across several regions, including the northwest, northeast and central regions.
The country is also battling a jihadist insurgency in its northeast that has lasted nearly two decades, drawing persistent criticism of the government's handling of insecurity.
Following the latest incident, police said they recovered 10 bodies with gunshot wounds after officers responded to a distress call.
The attackers had fled by the time they arrived but they continued to patrol the area to restore calm, they told BBC News on Saturday.

"We were able to disperse the unknown gunmen though there was no casualty on their side and ours because the terrain is difficult and they're used to the terrain," Assistant Superintendent of Police Victor Mshelizah said.
He added that officers were continuing to search the bush nearby for people who might have been killed or wounded, and warned the death toll could still rise.
Speaking to AFP news agency, community leader Malam Abubakar Saifullahi said the attackers had arrived on about 50 motorcycles, two men apiece.
"They looted shops and took cash, foodstuffs and other provisions," he said. "They also took motorcycles abandoned by people fleeing the attack."

articles.title: Veteran journalist Philip Lustre posts bail on cyberlibel raps
articles.summary: Lustre, 72, has posted bail amounting to P48,000 and was released on Saturday, October 24.

blocks.text: October 25, 2026 | 11:07am

Veteran journalist Philip Lustre Jr. is escorted by police officers at the Quezon City Police District (QCPD) Kamuning Station 10 in Quezon City to undergo physical and medical examination following his arrest on Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026.
The STAR / Miguel de Guzman
MANILA, Philippines — Veteran Journalist Philip Lustre has secured provisional liberty after posting bail on cyberlibel charges filed against him.
Lustre, 72, has posted bail amounting to P48,000 and was released on Saturday, October 24.
He was arrested on Saturday while attending a news forum based on a warrant of arrest issued by the Regional Trial Court, Branch 10, in Davao City.
According to Lustre’s lawyer, Dino de Leon, the veteran journalist was unaware of the complaint before his arrest.

“Per Mr. Lustre, he is unaware of any pending criminal charge or preliminary investigation against him prior to this arrest. As of writing, we still do not know the specific particulars of the case nor the identity of the complainant as the arrest happened on a weekend when the court that supposedly issued the warrant is closed,” De Leon said in a statement.

“In any event, we are looking at what appears to be a deprivation of Mr. Lustre’s right to due process at the preliminary investigation stage where no subpoena or notice was ever served on or received by him. In other words, he was not even given the chance to ventilate his defenses or air his side prior to the issuance of the warrant of arrest,” he added.

De Leon also pointed out that the arrest warrant listed an incorrect address: the Media Resource Plaza Building along Mola and Pasong Tirad Streets in Makati City, rather than Lustre's actual residence.
Lustre is the author of the book “Kill, kill, kill,” which tackled extrajudicial killings in the country.

In a separate statement, the Presidential Task Force on Media Security (PTFOMS) expressed concern over Lustre's October 24 arrest, urging authorities to respect his constitutional rights and grant him immediate access to legal counsel and medical care.

“PTFOMS takes serious note of concerns raised by media organizations that libel and cyberlibel laws have been weaponized to target critical voices, intimidate journalists, and discourage reporting on matters of public interest. These concerns call for careful review and effective safeguards against the abuse of legal processes,” the PTFOMS said.

articles.title: [Two Pronged] My love and sex life are complicated, and I want a committed relationship
articles.summary: Our letter sender is wondering about desire, life direction, and relationships as she finds someone she's compatible with sexually, but who can't stay in the Philippines and may not be able to commit…

blocks.text: Rappler’s People section runs an advice column by couple Jeremy Baer and clinical psychologist Dr. Margarita Holmes.

Jeremy has a master’s degree in law from Oxford University. A banker of 37 years who worked in three continents, he has been training with Dr. Holmes for the last 10 years as co-lecturer and, occasionally, as co-therapist, especially with clients whose financial concerns intrude into their daily lives.
Together, they have written two books: Love Triangles: Understanding the Macho-Mistress Mentality and Imported Love: Filipino-Foreign Liaisons.

Dear Dr. Holmes and Mr. Baer, I wonder these days why people enter relationships. While getting in one is not the center of my life, I have questions about the intersection between desire, life direction, and relationships.

I’m now at a point where I’ve experienced the most satisfying sex I could ever imagine with someone but he will not live in the Philippines permanently and when he leaves he knows he cannot maintain an LDR (long distance relationship).
I found myself in another two month relationship with a man with a volatile libido. I ended up walking on eggshells, crashing my libido badly.
I reconnected with the first guy. I was able to let my guard down and bare my raw self and act in a way that I’ve never been before.
Right now, this man is someone I can’t let go of but still I can’t just plan my life around him, so it’s a dilemma, a floating connection.
I now allow myself to talk to anyone that makes me happy. I don’t become loyal anymore to anything hypothetical and I have more reservations now.
I’m also deeply aware and learned the hard way that I don’t want to feel ever again that I’m good enough to f*** but not worthy enough to commit to.
– Anna
Dear Anna,
Relationships are complex and come in many forms, as it is clear you already know.

You ask why people enter them yet in reality you have answered your own question already. A relationship offers the opportunity to reveal yourself fully and safely with someone else without having to sacrifice your own dignity and integrity, an aim that is achievable but often only partially.
The two relationships you describe illustrate this. The “eggshell” one showed you what happens whenthere is no safety — having to deal with mood shifts can kill desire.

The “reconnection” one demonstrates the effect of safety – you can reveal your true self. The contrast is critical and can usefully inform your future. However, the way you describe your current attachment is scarcely ideal. He is someone you cannot let go of but cannot plan a future with either, or as you label it, this is a floating relationship.
That the sex is extraordinary is a bonus but also a distraction.
After all, great sex doesn’t mean that he is the right partner for you any more than a missing label means that he isn’t.
The real issue is: is he willing to move forward and label your relationship or are you shoring it up with hope that may be misplaced?

A way forward would be to ask him: what does he want from the relationship? Is he willing to build something? His answer, or avoidance, will tell you much more than any guesswork on your part and if in the final analysis he wants intimacy without commitment, at least you will know where you stand.
Best wishes,
– JAF Baer
Dear Anna:
Thank you very much for your letter. You ask a very important question: Why do people get into relationships?
A cursory search will give you a plethora of reasons, but in truth one can probably divide said reasons into two:

items: neuroscientific ones — mirror neurons, oxytocin, etc. but one of the simplest ways to describe this is that we are social beings that need relationships because our brains are wired to connect with others; and
practical and social reasons, such as when relationships result in children, it is much easier to raise the kids when said relationships continue; to avoid loneliness, etc.

blocks.text: From the theoretical standpoint above, let us now proceed to a more personal level and try to gain a larger perspective on your love and sex life.

At the moment, you seem to not just want, but actually need relationships with the opposite sex. In the last four months, you have been in a relationship first, with man A, whom you felt safe enough to have terrific sex with; but when his lack of commitment hurt you so much, you went to volatile man B who, thankfully, you realized after 2 months was not the sort of man you wanted in your life.

The following (4th) month, you went back to man A, not just because the sex was, once more, absolutely fantastic, but because you reveled in being the woman you felt you truly were (and you could well be right) when with him. And because you felt complete, cherished and truly seen by him, you wanted the relationship to continue.

Yet even as the relationship continued, man A was honest enough to say it couldn’t last forever because for whatever reason, he could not or would not stay in the Philippines forever. Man A, despite knowing that you could end the relationship prematurely (in his eyes-because I have a feeling not just the sex, but the while experience of being with you was also mind boggling for him), was honest enough to continue telling you the truth.
Some writers divide people into two types:
“Those who run away from something” or “Those who run towards something.”

Actually, I would include a third type of person: those who run towards something (like a seemingly perfect relationship with man A) but then realize it is best for their mental health to run away from that same something.
I would like to say that your last two paragraphs show what a mature person you have become. And this is true but, perhaps, not the complete truth.

If you can hold off from sex with someone you genuinely like whom you know also genuinely likes you, is willing to commit to you but is honest enough to say, but I am not sure if this commitment will be forever, then terrific.
You can still have a warm, funny, fulfilling relationship with him but not have sex.
Another option is to believe that just because a relationship (with sex) doesn’t last forever, it does not mean it is empty or worthless.
If you can truly manage one of these two options, then I say, “you go, girl!” But I am not sure you can.
This is not to demean you in any way. This is merely a recognition that people are different and some feel they need sex more than others.
If one is particularly blessed with the right experiences and/or the right therapy, one’s needs and one’s wants can live together harmoniously OR this can be a goal worth aspiring to.

And if one is self compassionate enough to forgive oneself for the same “mistakes” with the same generosity one could forgive one’s best friend, then each relationship you have can be a learning experience.
Hopefully, each relationship can also have more positive than negative elements in them.
That way, in time, you might agree with what the brilliant psychoanalyst and humanistic philosopher Erich Fromm once wrote in his 1956 book The Art of Loving:
Immature love: I love you because I need you.Mature love: I need you because I love you.
The best of luck to you – to US! — my fellow work in progress
– MG Holmes
Life got complicated? Write to our Two Pronged duo at twopronged@rappler.com.

articles.title: TRB all set to assist motorists during Undas 2026
articles.summary: The Toll Regulatory Board on Sunday said measures are in place to assist motorists as the country will observe All Saints' Day (Undas) and All Souls' Day on November 1 to 2, respectively.

blocks.text: Published October 25, 2026 10:58am
The Toll Regulatory Board (TRB) on Sunday said measures are in place to assist motorists as the country will observe All Saints' Day (Undas) and All Souls' Day on November 1 to 2, respectively.
TRB spokesperson Julius Corpus said "Oplan Biyaheng Ayos" will be implemented from October 29 to November 30 to ensure a smooth traffic flow along expressways.

He said all toll gates will remain open to avoid traffic congestion, while lane assistance personnel will be deployed to help motorists experiencing issues with their radio frequency identification (RFID) tags.

“We will also deploy additional patrol vehicles, toll trucks, fire trucks, ambulances, emergency medical service, and incident response teams to help motorists,” Corpus told Super Radyo dzBB in an interview.
He added that dedicated personnel will be deployed to manage the traffic inside service stations or stopovers and ensure clean and adequate facilities.
Free towing service will also be available, excluding repair service.
On Saturday, the Land Transportation Office (LTO) said there was still a normal flow of people at two major bus terminals in Metro Manila one week before the commemoration of Undas.
The LTO is implementing “Oplan Biyaheng Ayos” for Undas, inspecting Cubao, Quezon CIty and the Parañaque Integrated Terminal Exchange (PITX).
PITX is expecting around 1.9 million passengers this year amid the exodus for this year's All Saints' Day (Undas) break.
Many Filipinos are expected to go to their hometowns for the Undas break to pay their respects to their departed loved ones.
All Saints' Day will fall on Sunday, November 1, while All Souls' Day will be on Monday, November 2. Both are special non-working days. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: Obama attacks Trump as he campaigns for Democrats ahead of midterm elections
articles.summary: Obama said the election was "the last best chance to at least rein in some of the foolishness of this administration".

blocks.text: Former President Barack Obama has attacked the Trump administration over the Iran war and high consumer prices as he hit the campaign trail for Democrats ahead of the US midterm elections.
"This election is our last best chance to at least rein in some of the foolishness of this administration," Obama told crowds in Ohio on Saturday.
Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump touted his administration's immigration and tariff policies at a rally in Georgia, telling supporters "we're in the golden age of America".
The midterm elections on 3 November will decide which party controls Congress for the rest of Trump's term, and therefore how easy it is for the president to carry out his plans.
Early voting has already begun and Trump cast his ballot on Saturday in Florida alongside his wife First Lady Melania Trump.
Speaking on Saturday in Ohio and Michigan, Obama targeted Trump and his cabinet members, at one point mocking the president's attempt to redecorate the White House.

"After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in the modern era, you get a chance to say, 'enough is enough,'" the former president said in Cleveland.

Obama said he sympathised with voters who rejected Democrats in 2024 over economic and inflation concerns following the Covid pandemic. But he said Trump had only himself to blame for the current state of the economy.
"If you thought everything was too expensive before 'you know who'," he said, referring to Trump without using his name, "everything is more expensive now".
Trump, meanwhile, acknowledged that oil prices were "temporarily high" but said "our country is getting stronger and stronger all the time, and those pump prices are going to come down".
The Republican president has faced significant pressure to lower fuel prices, which have jumped due to the wars in Iran and Ukraine.

Talking up the economy, Trump told the crowd in Perry "we're taking in massive amounts of money through tariffs", and repeated his pledge to offer every adult American a $5,000 (£3,700) payout if Republicans win both chambers of Congress.
He also took aim at the Democrats, telling the crowd they would "loot your wealth" and "annihilate your borders".
Using derogatory language, he accused the Democrats of trying to open up immigration from Libya, Yemen, Haiti and Somalia - countries which he described as "terror-infested".

Describing a previous meeting with several senators, he recalled: "I said, 'Why do we always have to take people from shithouse countries? Why can't we take people from, like, well... Norway, Sweden? Why not Denmark?'"

articles.title: New York Archdiocese to pay $800 million to sex abuse survivors
articles.summary: Around 1,300 survivors agreed to the $800 million payout from the Catholic Church, marking one of the largest clergy abuse settlements in the US.

image.caption: Each of the survivors will receive at least $250,000, according to media reportsImage: Yuki Iwamura/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Survivors of sexual abuse by Catholic clergy accepted an $800 million (€714 million) settlement with the Archdiocese of New York, ending years of lawsuits, their lawyers announced on Saturday.

"The unanimous agreement of survivors who filed claims against the Archdiocese of New York marks a powerful moment in the pursuit of justice," Jeff Anderson, an attorney representing survivors, said in a statement.
"Through their courage, sacrifice, and determination, survivors have helped bring about a reckoning and a meaningful step toward accountability," it added.
The agreement was proposed by the Archdiocese of New York in May and is set to be formally signed in early November.
Each plaintiff to receive at least $250,000

Around 1,300 survivors are included in the agreement. Each of them is expected to receive at least $250,000, according to The New York Times, which broke the story. Some larger payouts are possible depending on the extent of the abuse.

"We are on the verge of being able to, please God, bring some measure of healing and reconciliation to all victim-survivors," New York Archbishop Ronald Hicks wrote in an email to clergy confirming the settlement.

"This agreement will also allow the archdiocese to turn its full attention once again to its mission of preaching the Gospel, healing the sick, caring for the poor and needy, welcoming the stranger, and educating our children," he added.

Hicks was appointed by the US-born Pope Leo in December 2025, replacing conservative Cardinal Timothy Dolan. Before leaving the post, Dolan had started a process of creating a $300 million fund to compensate victims of sexual abuse.
The deal announced on Saturday is one ​of the largest payouts over clergy sex abuse in ​the ‌US — second ‌only ​to an $880 million settlement reached by the Archdiocese of Los Angeles in 2024.
Catholic Church faces flurry of US abuse cases

articles.title: Myanmar’s Aung San Suu Kyi ‘sounds strong’ but is isolated, son says
articles.summary: Kim Aris tells the Guardian chance to speak with detained Nobel laureate was ‘public relations’ move from military leaders Myanmar’s former democratic leader Aung San Suu Kyi appears to be in good…

blocks.text: Myanmar’s former democratic leader Aung San Suu Kyi appears to be in good physical and mental health but is living in near-complete isolation, her son has said after the first call with his 81-year-old mother in more than five years.

“She still sounds certainly all there mentally, and physically she sounds strong,” Kim Aris said. “I don’t think she has anybody outside of the military or the police around her, so essentially she’s been held in solitary confinement from what I gather.”

After being deposed in a 2021 military coup, the Nobel Peace prize laureate has been moved to an unspecified location in the capital. “I’m still not entirely sure where she is,” said Aris. “I think it’s a residence in Naypyidaw, which is fenced off and it has a scrubby bit of land around it.”

blocks.caption: Aung San Suu Kyi talks on the phone with her son on Thursday, in a photo released by the Myanmar presidential office. Photograph: Myanmar President Spokesperson Office/AP

blocks.text: Aris, who has lived in the UK most of his life and whose late father was a British historian, was allowed to speak to his mother on Thursday at the Myanmar embassy in London. While he welcomed the chance to talk, he said the invitation was part of a “public relations” campaign by the country’s military leaders.

The former junta chief Min Aung Hlaing has sought to rebuild international diplomatic ties, and in April switched his military fatigues for civilian clothes after elections that were widely condemned as a sham.

Activists have long demanded “proof of life” for Aung San Suu Kyi, as well as scores of other political prisoners. In August, she was finally photographed during a Red Cross visit. Last week, a government spokesperson published images of her smiling in a wood-panelled room as officials delivered two gardening books given to her as gifts by Britain’s King Charles. A paper calendar on the wall behind her showed the date.

Aris said these photo-ops were well-known stunts that the regime had used before to pretend his mother, a national icon, was being treated fairly. The daughter of the assassinated national independence hero Gen Aung San has spent much of her life since the late 1980s in and out of house arrest for leading pro-democracy movements.

“She remains completely shut off from the rest of the world. I think she’s unaware of what’s happening outside of where she is because she’s not allowed any newspapers or radio or television,” Aris said. “She’s been locked up for five years on trumped-up, politically motivated charges and she should be free.”

Ruled for decades by generals and suffering from western sanctions, Myanmar experienced a brief democratic moment after Aung San Suu Kyi was allowed to run in a 2015 election that her party overwhelmingly won. She took up the role of “state counsellor” under a civilian-military power-sharing agreement.

blocks.caption: Aung San Suu Kyi shakes hands with Myanmar’s military commander-in-chief Min Aung Hlaing (left) in December 2015. Photograph: Lynn Bo Bo/EPA

blocks.text: Her international reputation was soon tarnished after the 2016-2017 mass killings and expulsions of Rohingya Muslims. Aung San Suu Kyi flew to the international court of justice in The Hague, where she said she acknowledged military units might have used “disproportionate force”, but defended the government against accusations of genocide.

Aris said that his mother was never “silent” on the Rohingya crisis and what she said on the issue “could fill volumes”. Under her leadership, Myanmar launched a domestic inquiry and appointed the former UN chief Kofi Annan to head a commission.
He added that as state counsellor, Aung San Suu Kyi was “always walking on a tightrope”, knowing the military could strip her of her fragile power at any moment.

“The very hard-won nascent democracy that she was trying to lead was holding on to things by a thread,” he said. “The military could have taken over at any point, and they were doing their best to make my mother’s situation a lot more difficult and to undermine her position. And I think in that respect they did a pretty good job.”
The 2021 power grab by the military triggered a civil war that has killed more than 100,000 people, according to conflict monitors.

Aris said the level of public global support for his mother had “dwindled incredibly” since the Rohingya crisis and that the whole country was now suffering from a lack of international attention. While many governments have called for Aung San Suu Kyi’s release, she is not treated as the beloved international figure that she once was.

“Never mind my mother, the fact that people ignore what’s happening in Burma shouldn’t be down to what was being done to the Rohingya,” he said, using the country’s former name. “And that seems to be the case sometimes, that people say: ‘Oh, well, look how the Rohingya were treated. We can ignore what’s happening in Burma.’”

articles.title: Where Philippine ducks gather, Apayao’s wild riches come into view
articles.summary: The findings will be used to guide habitat protection and wildlife monitoring while supporting responsible birdwatching and nature-based tourism

blocks.text: VULNERABLE. Philippine ducks, endemic Philippine waterbirds, are one of the species recorded in Santa Filomena in Apayao. DENR classifies it as 'vulnerable.'
DENR Cordillera
The findings will be used to guide habitat protection and wildlife monitoring while supporting responsible birdwatching and nature-based tourism

items: A three-day bird survey in Calanasan, Apayao, recorded over 427 birds from 23 species, including 322 Philippine ducks, highlighting the area's rich biodiversity.
The survey was conducted by the Department of Environment and Natural Resources-Cordillera in partnership with local governments and aimed to establish baseline data for conservation efforts.
The findings emphasize the importance of protecting Apayao's natural heritage as part of the UNESCO-designated Apayao Biosphere Reserve, which is home to various threatened species.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

BAGUIO, Philippines – Hundreds of Philippine ducks gathered in the wetlands of Calanasan, Apayao, where a three-day bird survey counted more than 300 of the endemic species together with threatened hornbills and other birds.

The survey recorded 427 birds from 23 species in the village of Santa Filomena, adding to scientific knowledge of a forest landscape in northern Luzon that is gaining recognition for its exceptional biodiversity.

Calanasan, the northernmost municipality of Apayao in the Cordillera region, is a landscape of extensive forests, winding rivers and mountain habitats. Its forests shelter the Philippine Eagle and other rare wildlife and plants, and form part of the Apayao Biosphere Reserve, designated by UNESCO in 2024.

blocks.caption: RAPTOR. A Brahminy kite (Haliastur indus), a raptor with a white head and breast and a chestnut-brown body, frequents rivers and coastlines and is listed as an other wildlife species in a forest area in Apayao. DENR-Cordillera

blocks.text: The survey was conducted by the Department of Environment and Natural Resources-Cordillera through its Community Environment and Natural Resources Office (CENRO) in Calanasan, in partnership with the municipal and provincial governments, local environment and tourism offices, and Provincial Green Guards.
The team set out to identify the bird species living in Santa Filomena, estimate their numbers and establish baseline data for future monitoring, habitat management and conservation.

Observations were made at Mawanan Resort and Casiggaman in Purok 7, and at Sinigpit and the Bridge Area in Purok 3, including sites near rivers and wetlands frequented by resident and migratory birds.
The most striking result was the number of Philippine ducks (Anas luzonica). Surveyors counted 322, making the species by far the most numerous recorded during the three-day survey.

blocks.caption: Rare giant bat turns up in Apayao forest monitoring

blocks.text: Endemic to the Philippines, the Philippine duck was classified as “vulnerable” on the country’s national list of threatened wildlife. Its presence in such numbers adds an important record to the growing picture of birdlife in Apayao, where forests and wetlands provide habitat for a remarkable range of species.
Its global status, however, was revised by the International Union for Conservation of Nature in 2025 from “vulnerable” to “least concern,” based on updated information and assessment.

The survey also recorded two other nationally threatened Philippine endemics: the rufous hornbill (Buceros hydrocorax), classified by the DENR as “endangered,” and the Luzon hornbill (Penelopides manillae), classified as “vulnerable.”

The survey report includes visual documentation of the Luzon hornbill and Philippine duck, together with species such as kingfishers, bee-eaters, herons, Brahminy kites, bulbuls, doves and the Philippine serpent eagle.

blocks.caption: BROWN. The brown-breasted kingfisher (Halcyon gularis), a Philippine endemic, is recognizable by its bright blue wings, large red bill and brownish breast. DENR-Cordillera

blocks.text: The sightings show birds using a range of habitats in Santa Filomena, from forest canopies and woodland edges to rivers, wetlands and open areas.

“The findings of the avifaunal survey in Barangay Sta. Filomena highlight Apayao’s rich biodiversity and reinforce our responsibility to protect its natural heritage as part of the Apayao Biosphere Reserve,” CENRO Calanasan officer-in-charge Dorothy Joy Cayaba told Rappler.
Cayaba said DENR-CAR intends to use the findings to guide habitat protection, wildlife monitoring and other conservation work while exploring responsible birdwatching and nature-based tourism.

The findings add to a series of notable biodiversity records from Calanasan. Philippine eagle nesting sites have been documented in the municipality, while recent botanical work identified endemic plants, including Medinilla calanasan and Vaccinium kilangensis. Some of these sites lie within the core zone of the Apayaos Biosphere Reserve.

UNESCO said the biosphere reserve covers about 3,960 square kilometers across Apayao and includes the Apayao Lowland Forest Key Biodiversity Area, known for its high levels of endemism and habitat for threatened species such as the Philippine Eagle.
Cayaba said CENRO Calanasan would continue working with local governments and community partners to translate the survey findings into conservation measures.

Future monitoring can help determine whether the large concentration of Philippine ducks and the presence of threatened hornbills persist over time, as well as which parts of Santa Filomena require the closest protection. – Rappler.com

articles.title: [Tambay] Ginoong Amba, dati na po kaming takot
articles.summary: Sabi ng ambassador ng Tsina, pasalamat daw ang Pilipinas at may kapit-bansa itong tulad ng Tsina na hindi gumagamit ng dahas. Teka, teka, hindi gumagamit ng dahas?

blocks.text: Asal sanggano itong bagong ambassador ng Tsina. Ito ang napuna ng grupo naming mga komentaristang kalye. Laman kasi ng mga legacy at social media ang tila pananakot ni Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan sa Pilipinas.

Nasabi kasi ni Amba na “pasalamat nga kayo hindi gumagamit ng dahas ang China” pagdating sa banggaan ng Tsina at Pilipinas sa West Philippine Sea. Ang basa ng mga kadaldálan ko, ang nakakubling mensahe nito ay “nagtitimpi lang kami sa inyo, huwag ninyo kaming subukan.”

Dito sa Pilipinas masama ang datíng ng binitawang salita ni Amba. Ganiyang-ganiyan ang linya ng mga kontrabida sa mga lumang pelíkulang Pinoy. Kadalasan sa mga sinaunang síne, pagkabigkas ng mga maton ng ganyang klase ng pagbabanta, susunod agad na eksena ay suntukang umaatikabo.
May nagbanggit doon sa kumpulan naming mga usisero, na ayon kay Amba Jing, hindi daw siya nananakot at “taken out of context” and “blown out of proportion.” Media daw ang may kagagawan.

Para naman fair kay Amba Jing, kinuha ko sa social media post ng Chinese Embassy Manila yung sinabi niya sa sideline ng isang forum kung saan naínterbiyu siya ng ilang reporter: “We should feel fortunate enough that you have a neighbor like China in this region. If we want to use force, we may easily win. But no, we will not choose force, and we love peace. In this region, we enjoy peace. Look at other regions: Ukraine, Gaza and even Venezuela. What happened there. We should cherish peace in this region.”

Peace o kapayapaan ba ika niya? Sa panayam na iyon, nasabi din ni Amba Jing yung mga Chinese language teacher at volunteer na kusang umuwi sa kanilang bansa dahil sa kaba sa personal nilang seguridad. Dinagdag din ni Amba na may mga hinuling manggagawang Tsino dito sa Pinas.

Pero nakalimutan niya yung mga binomba ng Chinese Coast Guard ng water cannon. Mga barko ng Philippine Coast Guard pinunteryá, at hindi gumanti ang mga kababayan natin. May mga binanggang barko ng PCG at ng Bureau of Fisheries.
Walang banggit din sa libo-libong higanteng barko ng Chinese militia na rumoronda sa loob ng West Philippine Sea. Wala rin siyang sinabi sa “freedom of navigation in the South China Sea.”

Inaangkin kasi ng Tsina ang halos buong karagatan na ito, kahit “international waters” ang turing dito ng maraming bansa. Pati nga mga isla na nasa loob ng bakuran ng Pinas, inaangkin ng Tsina. Nagpatayo rin ang Tsina ng base militar sa tabing bakúran natin sa karagatan.

Kay palad ng Pilipinas at kapit-bansa niya ang Tsina, ika ni Amba. “We love peace” sabi niya. Pero bakit nung Hulyo lumabas ang isang propaganda animation video sa China Daily na inihalintulad sa mga unggoy ang mga Pinoy.

Pakana ito ng estado ng Tsina, dahil nga lahat ng media at impormasyon sa kanilang bansa ay kontrolado ng pamahalaan. Sa video na iyon, minaliit ng Tsina ang panalo ng Pinas sa Hague ruling sa West Philippine Sea.

Ginoong Amba, masabi lang po ng tambay na ito nang may buong paggalang, hindi po naghahanap ng basag-ulo ang Pilipinas. Kabaliwan ang magpaka-basagulero ang Pinas diyan sa pinagtatalunang karagatan. Alam ng mga Pinoy na dehado kami kapag magkaroon ng bakbakan diyan. Gulpi ang aabutin namin. Hindi ninyo na po kailangan ipaalala iyan, Ginoong Amba.
Walang Pinoy na may tamang katinuan ang mag-aakalang may katiting na pag-asa tayo laban sa puwérsang Tsino.
Amba, hindi ninyo na po kailangang kaming takutin. Matagal na kaming takot. Dambuhala kontra bulilit ang sitwasyong iyan.
Pero huwag ninyo rin kaming mamaliitin. Hindi dahil ga-bubwit lang ang Pinas kumpara sa Tsina ay maari na ninyong gawin ang lahat ng gusto ninyo.
Kakasa kami para ipagtanggol ang sa amin. Kahit damulag ang manghimasok sa lugar namin, maninindigan kami. Hindi na usapan ng manalo-matalo iyan. Ipagtatanggol namin ang aming soberanya.

Nabanggit din lang naman ni Amba Jing ang “peace” kapansin-pansin ang pagbabago ng online persona ng Chinese Embassy Manila. Masigasig na mag-post ng sagot ang Chinese Embassy sa social media. Naiba na rin ang tono nito, mas agresibo.

Kapansin-pansin ang pagpíhit nito. Dati ang Ministry of Foreign Affairs ng Tsina na nasa Beijing ang mahilig manundot o manduro sa gobyerno ng Pilipinas, samantalang tikom ang bibig o kaya’y may diplomasya ang mga asal ng kanilang embahada sa Maynila. Pero ngayon, o mula ng dumating ni Ambassador Jing Quan, may sipa na ang mga komento sa social media ng Chinese Embassy of Manila.
Ang analisis ng isang kapwa kong nagdudunung-dunungan ay may basbas ng Chinese Communist Party ang kabangisan sa pananalita ni Amba at maging sa mga pahayag sa social media ng kanilang embahada.
Sa madaling salita, bukod sa pagiging marahas sa karagatan, ganoon na rin ang kanilang diskarte online. Kaya bardagulan sa West Philippine Sea, ay nasa karagatan at sa social media na rin.

Samantala, ang guwapo ng postura ni Senador Robin Padilla nung dumalo siya sa event ng Federation of Filipino-Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry. Yang mga pagdalo sa ganyang mga event, bahagi yan ng trabaho ng mga senador.
Sa mga photos sa FB page ni Senador Padilla, imbitado din sa piging si Amba Jing. Sabi ni Robin sa post niya:

“Alhamdulillah. Maraming salamat sa Federation of Filipino-Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry, Inc. sa kanilang imbitasyon na maging panauhin sa 2026 ASEAN Chinese Business Leaders Summit. Isang malaking pagkakataon ito upang makausap nang personal ang Ambassador ng China na si Ginoong Jing Quan. Edukado, gentleman, at diretsong kausap ang Ginoong Tsino. Mainam na maging personal at harapan ang pakikipag-usap sa kanya upang maiwasan ang hidwaan dulot ng mga palitan ng salita na hindi makapagdudulot ng kapayapaan at kaunlaran.”

Sa diretsong usapan ni Padilla at Amba, natanong kaya ng senador kung bakit ganoon ang trato ng China sa mga kapatid niyang Muslim sa Xinjiang. Sa talaan kasi ng United Nations nakatala ang kalupitan ng pamahalaan Tsina sa katutubong Uyghurs, na Muslim minority group sa Xinjiang.
Sana naitanong din ng senador kay Amba kung bakit ganoon din tratuhin ng Chinese Coast Guard ang kanilang counterpart na Philippine Coast Guard. – Rappler.com
Si Chito de la Vega ay Tambay ng Rappler dalawang beses kada buwan. Kasama rin siya sa mga anchor-host ng programang Balita Kwento Serbisyo ng DZME 1530.

blocks.text: October 25, 2026 | 9:12am
Pedestrians and motorists brave heavy rain along United Nations Avenue in Manila.
The Star / Ryan Baldemor
MANILA, Philippines — The Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) may bring rain to parts of the Visayas, Mindanao and Southern Luzon, the state weather bureau PAGASA said on Sunday, October 25.
In its daily weather forecast issued 4 a.m., PAGASA said the ITCZ may bring cloudy skies with scattered rain showers and thunderstorms to the Visayas, Mindanao, the Bicol Region, Romblon and Palawan.
The state weather bureau warned residents in these areas of possible flash floods or landslides due to moderate to, at times, heavy rains.
Meanwhile, Metro Manila and the rest of the country may experience partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rain showers or thunderstorms caused by localized thunderstorms.
PAGASA also warned residents in these areas of possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms.

articles.title: PH, Holy See mark 75 years of diplomatic ties, reaffirm commitment to peace, justice
articles.summary: The Philippines and the Holy See marked the 75th anniversary of their diplomatic relations on Friday with a Eucharistic celebration at the Santuario di San Giovanni Battista De La Salle in Rome,…

blocks.text: ROME — The Philippines and the Holy See marked the 75th anniversary of their diplomatic relations on Friday with a Eucharistic celebration at the Santuario di San Giovanni Battista De La Salle in Rome, reaffirming their shared commitment to peace, justice, and human dignity.

The Mass was presided over by Vatican Secretary of State Cardinal Pietro Parolin who highlighted the historical significance of the relationship and called for stronger dialogue and cooperation in addressing the challenges facing the world today.

The milestone also coincided with the 65th anniversary of the Pontificio Collegio Filippino in Rome, an institution dedicated to supporting the formation and studies of Filipino priests and seminarians.
Cardinal Parolin: Dialogue is essential to peace

In his homily, Cardinal Parolin recalled that diplomatic relations between the Philippines and the Holy See were formally established on April 8, 1951, during the pontificate of Pope Pius XII and the presidency of Elpidio Quirino.
He described the relationship as an indelible part of the shared history of the two sides, strengthened over the decades through mutual respect, religious ties, and diplomatic engagement.

Among the important milestones he highlighted were papal visits to the Philippines, visits by Philippine presidents to the Vatican, and the 2008 agreement concerning the cultural heritage of the Philippine Catholic Church.

Emphasizing the importance of diplomacy in a world marked by tensions and conflicts, Cardinal Parolin said, “In international relations, dialogue is an irreplaceable diplomatic tool for preventing conflicts and rebuilding bonds of trust.”
He urged both sides to continue strengthening their diplomatic ties and renewing their commitment to peace, justice, and the dignity of every human person.
“Whether we work in politics, diplomacy, culture, business, trade, or any other field, we are all called to be architects of peace and active builders of justice in today's world,” he said.
The cardinal also stressed the need to protect human dignity amid rapid technological development, warning that progress can benefit only a privileged few while leaving others behind.
“We must be the guardians of humanity, promoting the human dignity of all,” he emphasized.

Cardinal Pietro Parolin, Vatican secretary of state, recalls that diplomatic relations between the Philippines and the Holy See began on April 8, 1951, during his homily at a Mass held on the 75th anniversary of PH-Holy See diplomatic ties at the Santuario di San Giovanni Battista De La Salle in Rome on October 23, 2026. PIA GONZALEZ-ABUCAY
Church's growing Filipino leadership

In his remarks, Philippine Ambassador to the Holy See Raphael Perpetuo Lotilla reflected on the 75-year diplomatic relationship, highlighting the Holy See's continued support for Filipino participation and leadership in the Catholic Church.

“Significant in the 75 years of relationship has been the sustained support extended by the Holy See to deepen and reinforce Filipino participation and leadership in the Church in the Philippines,” Lotilla said.
He noted that the Catholic Church in the Philippines has developed a strong identity and leadership, with Filipino clergy and religious serving communities both at home and around the world.

Today, the Filipino Catholic community continues to contribute significantly to the life of the universal Church, reflecting the country's longstanding Catholic tradition and its growing international presence.
Pontificio Collegio Filippino celebrates 65 years

Lotilla also highlighted the 65th anniversary of the founding of the Pontificio Collegio Filippino in Rome, which provides Filipino priests and seminarians with opportunities for further studies and formation.

“The second milestone we are celebrating tonight is the 65th anniversary of the founding of the Pontificio Collegio Filippino in Rome, established to facilitate the studies of Filipino priests and seminarians,” he said.
The institution has played an important role in supporting the formation of Filipino clergy and strengthening their contribution to the Catholic Church in the Philippines and beyond.
Commemorative stamp
A highlight of the celebration was the unveiling of a commemorative postage stamp marking the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the Holy See and the Philippines.

The unveiling was led by Cardinal Parolin and Archbishop Emilio Nappa, secretary general of the Governorate of Vatican City State, alongside Philippine Secretary of Foreign Affairs Ma. Theresa P. Lazaro and Lotilla. The officials also signed the commemorative stamp to mark the occasion.

The stamp features St. Peter’s Basilica, an open shell containing a pearl symbolizing the Philippines as the “Pearl of the Orient Seas,” and the flags of both states. These elements reflect the shared Christian faith, enduring friendship, and longstanding cooperation between the two nations.

“This stamp, created by the Philatelic and Numismatic Office of the Vatican City State, celebrates the constant harmony, mutual enrichment, and shared purpose depicting this long friendship. It expresses in a single image our common Christian identity and the bonds of fraternity that unite us. It is a testament of a longstanding and solid tie of friendship and mutual cooperation,” said Archbishop Nappa.
Lazaro underscored the importance of faith in shaping the identity and values of the Filipino people.

“For the more than eighty-five million Filipino Catholics, our faith anchors our identity and values as Filipinos and collective nation. This commemorative stamp serves as a tangible symbol for the 75th anniversary of this establishment of diplomatic relations,” Lazaro said.
She noted that, like other postage stamps, the commemorative issue crosses borders, carries messages, and documents significant moments in history.

As nations navigate an increasingly complex world marked by technological advancements and uncertainties, Lazaro reaffirmed the Philippines’ commitment to peace, stability, and dialogue. She also emphasized the country’s continued cooperation with like-minded partners, including the Holy See, in addressing challenges that require collective action.

The event was attended by members of the diplomatic corps from various embassies, Philippine ambassadors to Southern European countries, priests, religious sisters, and members of the Filipino community.
The celebration concluded with a diplomatic reception, bringing together guests to commemorate the longstanding friendship and cooperation between the Holy See and the Philippines. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: California leaders rebuke Trump administration’s push over alleged noncitizen voting
articles.summary:
Election personnel concerned directive to ‘quickly’ verify 20,000 ballots could disenfranchise citizens

California’s top leaders have rebuked the Trump administration’s efforts to quash…

blocks.text: California’s top leaders have rebuked the Trump administration’s efforts to quash alleged noncitizen voting.
Less than two weeks before the midterms, federal prosecutors called upon California election officials to verify within 48 hours a list of about 20,000 ballots belonging to suspected noncitizens.

California’s election personnel have raised concern that the administration’s directive could disenfranchise citizens. Los Angeles officials said this week a “high percentage” of the individuals on the list were born in the United States.

“Trump’s DOJ is so desperate to invent ‘widespread voter fraud,’ it sent California counties lists of people who NEVER voted – and voters from the WRONG COUNTY. Absolute clown show!” California’s governor Gavin Newsom posted on social media.
“Voter intimidation has no place in our democracy,” Pete Aguilar, a congressman representing south-west San Bernardino county, said in a social media post.
The federal government’s oversight attempts come amid a national Republican effort to crack down on alleged voter fraud, particularly any cases among undocumented immigrants.

“We are asking each county election official to commit to working with us by providing the necessary information for DHS to quickly verify citizenship status. With their help, we can ensure the most secure election in California history,” the justice department said.
Rob Bonta, the California attorney general, has raised questions about the evidence behind the suspected noncitizen ballots.

“All they provided was a list of people and nothing about why they’re purportedly ineligible. If they have such information, we would be happy to review it, but they’ve provided none,” Bonta said at a recent press conference.
The DoJ also charged 28 foreign nationals recently, accusing them of fraudulently registering to vote.

“Today’s arrests prove what we have been saying,” Bill Essayli, first assistant US attorney, said in a statement. “California is mailing ballots to noncitizens, and they are refusing to comply with federal law, which makes it a crime for noncitizens to vote. The voting rights of American citizens must be protected.”
Some state officials took no action, citing the fast-approaching election, which spurred a legal battle with the justice department. An appeals court is set to hear the matter on Tuesday.
