articles.title: Almost 1,000 arrested as clashes follow another day of mass protests across France
articles.summary: Officials have so far managed to avoid a repeat of last weekend's rioting and looting as hundreds of thousands took part in demonstrations.

blocks.text: Some 70,000 police officers were deployed and restrictions imposed in several cities to prevent the latest protests over the cost of living and poor school conditions from descending into the kind of chaos which saw officers outnumbered, hundreds of businesses looted and buildings torched.

President Emmanuel Macron had decreed earlier this week that only demonstrations organised by a recognised trade unions would be permitted. Hundreds of people have been jailed for vandalism, arson and looting after fast-track court hearings in recent days.

Clashes between protesters and riot police in Paris erupted at the end of a peaceful march from the city's Porte d'Italie towards Porte de Vincennes on Saturday, where the police operation included an elite unit that usually deals with organised crime and counter-terrorism.
Some protesters were seen erecting makeshift barricades and pelting officers with projectiles, while police baton-charged groups of masked youths who were smashing the windows of a car dealership.

French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said that "several thousand radical activists gathered at the rear of the march, including around 500 individuals identified as rioters", the AFP news agency reported.

In the southern port of Marseille, rubbish bins were set ablaze and metal sheets used to block streets. A law enforcement vehicle was seen driving through a burning barricade in France's second-largest city.
Meanwhile, some protesters in dark clothing and face coverings were seen taking boards off a building to build a street barricade in the southern city of Bordeaux.
In Lyon, police used tear gas grenades to disperse a crowd which had reportedly gathered in an area deemed off-limits by the local prefecture.

"There were around 150 of us, mostly secondary school and university students. Then the tear gas came almost immediately. You could barely see anything in the street," said one protester in France's third-largest city.
Nuñez said late in the day that nearly 1,000 people had been arrested, a number he said would increase.
The minister also said two people had been "seriously injured": one in the south-western city of Toulouse, and another one in Clermont-Ferrand, central France.

Earlier, a peaceful protester in Paris who gave her name as Zelie told the BBC people had taken to the streets because they were "really frustrated" and had been "suffering a lot" since Macron came to office.
"They keep us quiet. They take our money, they tax us a lot and we can't say anything. Today we are in the streets because it's been too long, it's been too much," the 26-year-old said.
Two masked teenage protesters, who did not want to give their names, also said their generation was in despair and felt abandoned by the government.
"I think looting is really not good," one of the demonstrators said of last Saturday's disorder. "But it's because of poverty and the violence of the police."
He added that the protests would end "when we have a response to our demands. We really want a change in France".
Meanwhile, some 13,000 people joined a rally against the hard-right National Rally party in the north-central city of Orléans which proceeded peacefully.
Mass protests triggered by similar issues as in France also rocked several other European cities on Saturday.
In Albania's capital Tirana, riot police fired tear gas to disperse thousands of anti-government demonstrators, while clashes were also reported in Belgium's capital Brussels.

In Milan, northern Italy, a major security operation including hundreds of soldiers alongside police prevented protesters gathering in the city. Many had feared a repeat of violent scenes last week when some started fires, smashed windows and looted shops.

Around 550,000 people took part in last weekend's demonstrations against rising fuel prices and the cost of living, with frustrations escalating after weeks of student protests. The chaos which followed resulted in more than 2,500 arrests.

Marches were initially largely peaceful but became marred by scenes of violence, looting and destruction, with more than 2,000 shops and other businesses across France said to have been directly impacted. The damage was estimated "at hundreds of millions euros", France's Chambers of Commerce and Industry (CCI) said.
One demonstrator's hand was blown off by a police crowd-control grenade, according to the AFP news agency, while about 1,000 police officers were injured.
The French authorities later said they were forced to impose overnight curfews in Paris and other cities.
The continuing protests come ahead of France's presidential elections in six months' time, and leading contenders have levelled the blame at Macron and his ministers.

articles.title: Convicted murderer who attended McGill's faculty of law now back in custody
articles.summary: Jeffrey George Ewert, a convicted murderer who has stirred controversy while attending law courses at McGill University, is back in custody while authorities look more closely at his case.
articles.byline: Sidhartha Banerjee, Leah Hendry, Benjamin Shingler

image.caption: McGill University in Montreal, where Jeffrey George Ewert began attending law school in August. (Kolya Hubacek-Guilbault/CBC)

blocks.text: Montreal·Breaking
Jeffrey George Ewert, a convicted murderer who has stirred controversy while attending law courses at McGill University, is back in custody while authorities look more closely at his case.
Jeffrey George Ewert, who was out on day parole, has been arrested on a warrant, CBC confirms
· CBC News
· Posted: Oct 24, 2026 4:52 PM EDT | Last Updated: 8 minutes ago
A convicted murderer who has stirred controversy while attending law courses at McGill University is back in custody while authorities look more closely at his case.
The Correctional Service of Canada (CSC) confirmed to CBC News on Saturday that a suspension warrant for Jeffrey George Ewert was issued.

“The offender has returned to custody while a more thorough assessment of the situation is being conducted,” the statement said. Two sources had confirmed to CBC that Ewert had been picked up on Friday.
Ewert was convicted of second-degree murder and attempted murder for attacks against two women in B.C. in 1984 and is serving a life sentence.

He was granted day parole in 2025 and began taking law classes and going to faculty events at the Montreal institution in August. He had not been on campus since early October, according to a statement from McGill's provost.

His parole was extended for another six months in June 2026. While various clinical assessments ranked Ewert’s risk of reoffending as moderate to high, official parole documents say with close supervision at a halfway house and clinical follow-up, that risk “seems to fall more into the moderate risk category.”

items: Duelling petitions highlight rift over paroled murderer at McGill law school
McGill law school grapples with fallout after paroled murderer excluded from campus

blocks.text: The parole board did express concern about his interactions with and attitudes toward women.

In a statement Saturday, the federal agency that oversees adult offenders said a conditional release can be suspended in situations where there are “reasonable grounds to believe that the offender has breached a condition of release or that the risk they present can no longer be safely managed in the community.”
The case will be reviewed with the established post-release decision-making process, the agency said. That could include further consideration by the Parole Board of Canada (PBC).
The CSC says given it is an active case, it can’t comment further or provide further information about what led to the suspension as per the Privacy Act.
Presence stirs debate at McGill
But his attending McGill has created a deep divide over the presence of a convicted killer in the classroom.
One petition has circulated outlining why students feel unsafe and don’t want to be in Ewert’s presence. The petition expressed concern over his alleged behaviour while attending McGill.
However another petition argued that excluding Ewert from campus undermines his access to education and rehabilitation as an Indigenous man and a survivor of the Sixties Scoop.
The CSC says information about an offender's time in the community is continually gathered.
“When concerns arise regarding an offender's behaviour, compliance with release conditions, or ability to be safely managed in the community, CSC takes appropriate action,” the CSC said.

“If the risk can no longer be safely managed in the community, CSC may suspend the offender's release and return them to custody. CSC works closely with its partners to respond quickly when circumstances require intervention.”
In a statement to CBC on Friday, a spokesperson for McGill said the "safety and security of our students is paramount."
The university also promised to "actively review its admissions processes to ensure a similar situation never happens again."
Convicted killer attending McGill law school divides students over safety, 2nd chances
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Sidhartha Banerjee is an assignment editor based in Montreal. He previously worked at The Canadian Press and The Montreal Gazette. He can be reached at sidhartha.banerjee@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Six Flags to reopen Goliath rollercoaster – but now with seatbelts after recent rider death
articles.summary:
Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem fell from ride earlier this month, spurring amusement park to temporarily shut it down

Six Flags will install seatbelts on its Goliath rollercoaster in

blocks.text: Six Flags will install seatbelts on its Goliath rollercoaster in Georgia, after a rider plummeted to his death earlier this month.

Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, a 42-year-old father and educator, was thrown from his seat on the Goliath, a coaster that plunges riders down 165ft, before a second drop of 180ft. On his way down, he collided with the ride’s other cars.
Georgia authorities have launched a probe into Kariem’s death. The gruesome fall prompted the park to temporarily close the Goliath and eight rides at five other parks.
“What happened has deeply affected all of us at Six Flags. Safety has always been fundamental to the experience we provide for our guests,” the theme park’s CEO, John Reilly, wrote on Friday.

Seatbelts will also be added to coasters with a similar restraint, he announced, although an exact list remains unclear. The Goliath features a lap bar that locks over a rider’s waist, a design from Bolliger & Mabillard.
The park has also commissioned an independent review of the safety procedures for all of its attractions.
“I know trust is earned through actions and not words,” Reilly said. “We will continue to communicate about our progress and hold ourselves accountable to our commitments to you.”

The Six Flags Over Georgia fatal incident comes as the theme park is being sued over alleged bodily harm from its X2 ride at Magic Mountain. A recent CNN investigation uncovered a long history of brain injuries and at least two deaths linked to the ride.

A group of past riders who say they sustained brain injuries on X2 has accused the park of having a defective coaster and negligence for allowing its continued operation, according to court documents.
Six Flags permanently shut down the embattled X2 coaster in September.

articles.title: Ukraine: Starlink satellite speeds restored to normal
articles.summary: The announcement comes after Starlink and Starshield restrictions had disrupted military operations in Ukraine and sparked tensions with the US.

image.caption: Ukrainian soldiers handle a Starlink terminalImage: Dmytro Smolienko/Ukrinform/Avalon/Photoshot/picture alliance

blocks.text: The Starlink satellite system and its military version Starshield were fully functional on Saturday, the Ukrainian government said.
Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said speeds for Starlink and Starshield started returning to normal overnight.
Ukraine's ‌defense ministry confirmed on Saturday that the connection remained stable at over 400 kilometers per hour (kph).
"The main thing for today is ‌that Starlink and Starshield have resumed operations at their pre-restriction speeds. The speeds are now at the level we need," Zelenskyy said on Telegram.
"This is crucial. This really matters: for our frontline logistics, for defending Ukraine against jet-powered 'Shaheds,'" he added.
The announcement comes after over a week of Starlink and Starshield restrictions that disrupted military operations in Ukraine and sparked tensions with the US.
Ukrainian officials said that the capped speeds of 160 kph had hampered the military's ability to intercept Russian attack drones and forced the cancellation of some operations.
Did someone order Ukraine's high-speed Starlink shutdown?
What caused Starlink's restrictions?
Starlink is operated by rocket company SpaceX, owned by billionaire Elon Musk, who is a close ally of US President Donald Trump.

US newspaper The Wall Street Journal (WSJ) reported earlier this week that US officials believed Musk acted unilaterally in capping the speeds at which Ukrainian hardware could stay connected to the satellite-based network.
According to the WSJ report, officials signaled that Trump did not specifically order retribution against Kyiv.
But in response to the report, Musk said that "any limits to speed or usage" of Starshied were "decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS."
Both Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth have denied that the Pentagon had directed any changes.
It remains unclear who is responsible for last week's Starlink slowdown.
Kyiv has come to question Washington's support over intelligence sharing, amid speculation that the White House may have ordered the restrictions on Starshield.

The Starlink slowdown came as the relationship between the US and Ukraine has become strained after President Donald Trump's reported deal with Moscow on Russian diesel imports, which Ukraine viewed as a betrayal.

blocks.text: Toronto
Toronto police are seeking the public’s help in locating three missing children, allegedly abducted by their mother from the Midland Avenue and Eglinton Avenue East area.
Children allegedly abducted during semi-supervised visit with family
Daniel, 6, Irina, 3, and four-month-old Anastasia were having a semi-supervised visit with a relative on Friday, when their mother took them and fled the premises, police said Saturday.
Their mother, Somerda Miclescu, 22, is believed to be driving a 2017 White Ford Expedition SUV with Ontario licence plate DJJS 875, according to police.

From left, Daniel, 6, Irina, 3, and four-month-old Anastasia were having a semi-supervised visit with a relative on Friday, when their mother took them and fled the premises, police say. (Toronto Police Service)
The mother does not have legal custody of the children and her location is unknown, police said.
Police described her as 5-7, around 180 pounds, with long, dark black hair. Police say she was last seen wearing a long black skirt and a dark-coloured top.
Police had first responded to a call on Friday at around 11:30 a.m. for an abduction in the Midland Avenue and Eglinton Avenue East area.
Ionut Stroe, 25, is also wanted as a person of interest for owning the vehicle Miclescu fled in.
Unrelated to the alleged abduction, police say Stroe is currently wanted for four counts of failing to comply with a release order.
Police described him as being around 5-11, 235 pounds, with a tattoo on his right forearm.
Ionut Stroe, 25, is also wanted by police as a person of interest for owning the vehicle Somerda Miclescu fled in. (Toronto Police Service)
No Amber Alerts are being issued at this point, according to Insp. Jeff Allington at a news conference Saturday.
Anyone with information is asked to contact police directly at 416-808-4100.

articles.title: Tens of thousands of Lula supporters rally on eve of Brazilian election runoff
articles.summary:
Nearly 159 million people to head to polls on Sunday in battle between leftwing incumbent and Flávio Bolsonaro

Tens of thousands of supporters of Brazil’s leftwing president, Luiz Inácio…
articles.byline: Tom Phillips in Rio de Janeiro and Tiago Rogero in Belo Horizonte

blocks.text: Tens of thousands of supporters of Brazil’s leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, have streamed on to Rio’s most famous beach for a giant protest they hope will propel him towards a historic election fightback against his far-right rival, Flávio Bolsonaro.
Nearly 159m Brazilians will vote in the election’s runoff on Sunday, with the pair tied in the polls after Bolsonaro won the first round on 4 October by 47% to 45%.

On Saturday, under a fierce sun, red-clad crowds packed the 2.5-mile Copacabana beach in an attempt to help Lula clinch a dramatic and unprecedented comeback. Never since the return of democracy to Brazil in the 1980s has the first-round loser managed to bounce back.

Josias Silva, a 61-year-old truck driver, voiced confidence that his 80-year-old president would win a fourth non-consecutive term. He carried a homemade sign to the carnival-like procession reading: “Lula re-elected. Tomorrow will be a new day.”

blocks.caption: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva waves to supporters on Saturday. Photograph: Dhavid Normando/AP

blocks.text: “The people have woken up,” Silva said of the large pro-Lula street protests that have swept Brazil since the leftist’s first-round defeat, many led by students.

“Young people know we need this victory because otherwise we will have dictatorship again – and we don’t want dictatorship. We don’t want hatred. We don’t want guns. We want a country of love,” added Silva, celebrating the large number of people who came to witness one of the final presidential campaign rallies in Lula’s storied 50-year political career.
“There’s never been a demonstration like this one. This is the biggest protest in the history of Brazil. And we are going to win tomorrow with more than 60% of the votes,” Silva claimed.

Polls suggest a far tighter margin and most analysts see Bolsonaro, whose father, Jair Bolsonaro, was president from 2019 to 2022, as the slight favourite, having sold himself to voters as someone who will tackle chronic levels of violent crime with an iron fist.

However, in recent days Lula has appeared to regain the initiative and climb in the polls, amid a succession of scandals involving his rightwing foe. Last week the Brazilian magazine Piauí claimed that at the height of Brazil’s 2020 coronavirus outbreak, Flávio Bolsonaro attended a boat party attended by sex workers and vaccine lobbyists hoping to strike a deal with the government of his father.

blocks.caption: People watch a televised debate between Flávio Bolsonaro and his election rival on Friday. Photograph: Adriano Machado/Reuters

blocks.text: Some experts speculate a Lula comeback may be possible. At the Copacabana rally, activists unfurled an enormous yellow and green banner declaring: “WE ARE GOING TO TURN THIS AROUND!”
“I’m super excited. Lula’s going to win,” said Marta Moraes, a 59-year-old restaurateur, as she joined Saturday’s demo.

Moraes said the election was not about left versus right. “We’ve nothing against the right … what we’re against is Bolsonarismo,” she said, tears filling her eyes as she recalled how Flávio Bolsonaro’s father botched the response to Covid during his chaotic 2019-2022 administration.
“I lost four members of my family because of Bolsonaro’s neglect,” Moraes said.

blocks.caption: Lula supporters on Copacabana Beach in Rio de Janeiro. Photograph: Agustín Marcarian/Reuters

blocks.text: Jair Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year prison sentence for plotting a coup after he lost the 2022 election to Lula. Many Brazilian democrats fear he will be released – and could even return to government – if his son wins. Reports in the Brazilian press suggest several of Bolsonaro’s fellow plotters – who are now in prison or hiding in exile – may be given top military and police jobs in a Bolsonaro administration.
Cammy Marinho, a 49-year-old DJ and activist, said: “I’m here to prevent democracy becoming extinct – which is what the Bolsonaro family wants”.
Marinho said she had spent the past fortnight fighting to persuade people who voted for Bolsonaro, or did not vote in the first round, to back Lula.

“It’s non-stop work: in the bakery, in the supermarket, on the underground – whenever you feel there is an opening to talk to someone and show to them the reality, everything that Lula has done and is doing for the people and everything that this [Bolsonaro] family has done against the people,” she said.
Many marchers were part of the so-called “Lula’s Army” – a 10 million-member WhatsApp group that was created after the first round in the hope of turning the election around.
“Being a soldier in Lula’s army … means fighting for Brazilian democracy. This isn’t a normal election,” said Isabella Gaze, 64, a retired teacher and one of the group’s members.

“They constantly claim Lula is corrupt. But the truth is that they represent the most rotten and worst part of Brazilian politics. This is what we are fighting against now,” Gaze said of the Bolsonaros.

Many of the faces on Copacabana beach were teenagers, including 14-year-old Heitor Lopes da Silva. Silva had come from the city of Duque de Caxias in his wheelchair, with a placard that said: “Lula, I’m a person with a disability and I’m here to support you.”
“My whole life I’ve believed Lula was a good president. [Bolsonaro] represents the destruction of Brazil …. he represents sadness and death,” he said of the Bolsonaro-era Covid catastrophe.

blocks.caption: Some Lula supporters believe he can overturn the lead his rival secured in the first round of voting. Photograph: Agustín Marcarian/Reuters

blocks.text: Large crowds of Bolsonaro supporters also hit the streets, including in Belo Horizonte, the capital of Minas Gerais state, which has Brazil’s second-largest electorate after São Paulo, and is a key bellwether. No presidential candidate has ever won the presidency without securing Minas Gerais, where Bolsonaro led by just under 5% in the first round.

Thousands of Bolsonaristas gathered to see their candidate in a palm-lined plaza called Praça da Liberdade. To the booming sound of AI-generated funk carioca tracks praising Bolsonaro, a sea of supporters dressed in Brazil’s yellow football jersey waved Brazilian flags – and many of the United States too.
“The US is a great nation. Who wouldn’t want to be aligned with them?” said 56-year-old cosmetics entrepreneur Marcos Antonio, holding a flag that merged the emblems of both countries.

“I don’t want an alliance with Cuba or Venezuela. I want to move forward,” Antonio added. When reminded that Venezuela was currently aligned with the US after Donald Trump’s January invasion, he said: “True. But for now, a fully right-wing government hasn’t been installed yet. It’s in transition.”

blocks.caption: Bolsonaro supporters, some with the flags of the US, Israel and Brazil, also held last-minute rallies on Saturday. Photograph: Raquel Cunha/Reuters

blocks.text: Antonio Carlos Costa Jr, the 59-year-old owner of a shooting club, complained: “Lula did nothing for the country.”

Jair Bolsonaro relaxed gun ownership and buying laws – which security experts agree ended up diverting many firearms to criminal gangs – whereas Lula tightened regulations once again. “Jair Bolsonaro simply gave citizens the right to defend themselves, and his son will do the same,” said Costa Jr.
Lula supporters scoff at the idea that Bolsonaro, who has a history of well-documented ties with members of Rio’s paramilitary “militia” groups, could rid Brazil of criminality.
“If we vote the militias into power, we will be living in a dictatorship,” said Erika Cavalcante, 43, an architect who came to the march with a sign reading: “Don’t let the mobsters win.”

articles.title: Hundreds of thousands march across France in protests over schools and policing
articles.summary:
Government estimates at least 400,000 people took part, but trade unions say the number is double that

Hundreds of thousands marched in cities across France on Saturday in largely peaceful…

blocks.text: Hundreds of thousands marched in cities across France on Saturday in largely peaceful protests to support schoolchildren’s demands for more teachers and repairs to dilapidated buildings, as Emmanuel Macron faces a social and political crisis in his final months as president.

In Paris, at least 110,000 people marched along the eastern edge of the city, according to government estimates. They supported high schoolers but also complained of the high cost of living and the government’s heavy policing, saying riot police had been sent to target school protesters over the past month, instead of the government offering political solutions.

The mood in Paris on Saturday afternoon was peaceful and lighthearted, with brass bands playing and children and grandchildren present. Some people carried banners critical of the government’s policing, saying: “Oppression breeds rebellion” and “The right to protest”.

But at the end of the Paris demonstration, at Porte de Vincennes on the city’s eastern edge, different groups of masked men dressed in black emerged who had not appeared to have taken part in the peaceful march. Some groups of masked men threw glass bottles and stones at police, who responded with teargas, water cannon and stun grenades. A bin was set alight and fireworks were set off towards police.
Police also fired teargas to prevent protesters in Lyon, Lille, Montpellier, Nantes and Toulouse from reaching city centres. In Marseille, some bin fires were lit amid clashes with police.
The government estimated that at least 400,000 people had marched across France. Trade unions estimated the number at double that.

More than 70,000 police were on the streets of French cities, with shops boarded up and many museums closed. The government had feared a repeat of last Saturday, when, despite peaceful protests taking place, France saw one of the most violent days of unrest in years with public buildings burned, hundreds of shops destroyed and looted and at least 2,700 people arrested in cities across the country.
At Saturday’s protests, there was widespread anger at Macron for banning non-union demonstrations that his government deemed “illegitimate” and for keeping all protesters away from city centres.

blocks.caption: At the end of the Paris demonstration, different groups of masked men dressed in black emerged and threw glass bottles and stones at police. Photograph: Thibault Camus/AP

blocks.text: At the Paris march, Nadège, a 43-year-old communications worker, said she had been teargassed last weekend at a peaceful demonstration. “I’m out again peacefully today to support everyone who is brave enough to demonstrate. It does take courage. People are afraid now. We have to keep our rights alive … In France, it’s our legal right to protest in the street and I’m here to defend that.”

One 21-year-old student from a Paris science faculty that is currently blockaded by demonstrators said: “We feel in France that we are increasingly living in an authoritarian regime that is trying to stop our democratic right to protest in the street.”

The government has been facing a crisis since the start of high school demonstrations in mid-September, when children aged between 15 and 18 began protesting against staff shortages at their schools, leaking and crumbling buildings, and a lack of chairs in overcrowded classrooms. It grew into the biggest youth movement in years, with trade unions, teachers and parents joining. Police investigations are under way after some children and protesters were maimed and injured by explosive police weaponry.

At Saturday’s march there were some people dressed in yellow vests who had taken part in the gilets jaunes anti-government protests of 2018 and 2019. Standing amid demonstrators, Jérôme Rodrigues, a key figure from the gilets jaunes protest, said: “Today the government is afraid; that is why they are pushing demonstrators to the edge of the city, away from places of power. It’s not police shields that will provide an answer to French people struggling and unable to make ends meet.” He said it was likely that demonstrations would continue each weekend.
after newsletter promotion

Pierre, 60, a retired banking consultant, said he was demonstrating in support of school students. “I have an eight-year-old granddaughter. I want her to have a brighter future than the sombre times we are facing today. There is a complete refusal by the government to listen to people’s demands.”

Jesse, 40, a charity worker from the north of Paris, carrying a sign saying “Free Hugs”, said: “I’m so angry. I’m here to support schoolchildren’s demands for better conditions. I’m so proud of them and we have to stand together.”

She said: “I know I’m not going to war by coming out to demonstrate peacefully. But at times it really does feel like a war … This is the first time I’ve prepared so carefully for a peaceful march, wearing old clothes in case they are gassed or torn.”

In Orléans, thousands of people shouting anti-fascist slogans marched against a congress being held by Marine Le Pen’s far-right anti-immigration the National Rally party. Protesters criticised Le Pen, who is a frontrunner in next year’s presidential election, as well as Macron, who steps down from power next year. “Macron, resign. Le Pen in prison,” the crowd shouted.

The interior minister, Laurent Nunez, said 135 people had been arrested in France and weapons had been confiscated, including metal balls, lead pellets, fireworks, slingshots, steel balls, improvised weapons, a katana sword and airsoft weapons.

articles.title: Napolcom warns erring criminology interns
articles.summary: National Police Commission (Napolcom) Commissioner Rafael Vicente Calinisan warned criminology interns on Saturday that violating traffic rules, including riding motorcycles without helmets, could…

blocks.text: Published October 25, 2026 12:29am

National Police Commission (Napolcom) Commissioner Rafael Vicente Calinisan warned criminology interns on Saturday that violating traffic rules, including riding motorcycles without helmets, could jeopardize their applications to become police officers.

In a Facebook post, Calinisan urged the public to photograph criminology interns caught violating traffic regulations, saying authorities would identify them and refuse to process their applications for police service or entertain them in Napolcom examinations.

“Yang mga ‘Criminology Interns’ na mga walang helmet at nagba-violate ng traffic rules, take their photos. We will get their names, identify them, and we will NOT process their application as policemen or entertain them in the NAPOLCOM Exams,” he said.

(I urge the public to take photos of those "criminology interns" who ride motorcycles without helmets and violate traffic rules. We will obtain their names, identify them, and we will NOT process their applications to become police officers or allow them to take the NAPOLCOM examinations,” he said.
Calinisan’s warning comes amid recurring online complaints about alleged traffic violations by criminology students as Napolcom pushes to tighten police recruitment and improve criminology education.

Republic Act No. 6975, as amended by Republic Act No. 8551 or the Philippine National Police Reform and Reorganization Act of 1998, empowers Napolcom to establish policies and criteria for the recruitment and selection of police personnel.

The Napolcom commissioner called for reforms in the training of aspiring police officers and urged criminology schools to help identify and weed out students who display a sense of entitlement and disregard for the law.

“Nananawagan ako sa mga (I am appealing to) Criminology Schools: help us by weeding out these entitled individuals as early as possible. Di dapat sila maging pulis (They should not become police officers),” he said.

Calinisan also called on schools to improve their curricula and guard against operating as diploma mills, adding that producing responsible police officers was part of a broader responsibility to the nation.

“Salain ang dapat salain. Ayusin ang curriculum. Wag diploma mill (Screen those who need to be screened. Improve the curriculum. Do not operate diploma mills). Nationbuilding is everyone's responsibility,” he said.—MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Musk says he was behind Starlink speed restriction in Ukraine
articles.summary: Elon Musk said on Saturday that his company SpaceX had throttled the Starlink satellite internet service in Ukraine, disrupting operations that the country relies on to defend itself against Russia.

image.caption: Elon Musk said on Saturday that his company SpaceX had throttled the Starlink satellite internet service in Ukraine, disrupting operations that the country relies on to defend itself against Russia. (Evan Vucci, Dado Ruvic/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·Updated
Elon Musk said on Saturday that his company SpaceX had throttled the Starlink satellite internet service in Ukraine, disrupting operations that the country relies on to defend itself against Russia.
Announcement comes as Kyiv says satellite speeds restored after days of issues

Musk's admission on social media came after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that Ukraine's access to Starlink and Starshield satellite links has been restored to the speeds it had before restrictions that disrupted front-line operations for more than a week.
Questions have persisted since last week about who ordered the interruptions to the Musk-made satellite internet system that Kyiv has relied on for years to counter Moscow's attacks.

"The speeds are now where they need to be," Zelenskyy wrote on X, adding that restoration began overnight and were sufficient by Saturday morning, improving front-line logistics and defence against Russian jet-powered Shahed drones.

After Ukraine said the services had been restored, Musk spoke out on the speed restrictions that began last week. In a post Saturday on X, Musk acknowledged that his company SpaceX throttled the Starlink satellite internet service.

"Using Starlink, a civilian commercial service, for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed, nor should it be," Musk wrote. "Ukraine military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week."

But he maintained that the U.S. government controlled whatever changes happened with Starshield, the military-grade version of Starlink that is the backbone of Ukraine's drone operations and communication. He also defended the role of SpaceX in bolstering Ukraine's defences since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

articles.title: Revilla bid to inhibit justice junked anew
articles.summary: The Sandiganbayan has upheld its earlier ruling denying former senator Ramon Revilla Jr.’s bid to stop one of its justices – who specifically ruled to deny him P1 million bail –…

blocks.text: October 25, 2026 | 12:00am
Former senator Bong Revilla at the Department of Justice as he filed his counter-affidavit on his plunder complaint on Feb. 12, 2026.
Philstar.com / Ian Laqui

MANILA, Philippines — The Sandiganbayan has upheld its earlier ruling denying former senator Ramon Revilla Jr.’s bid to stop one of its justices – who specifically ruled to deny him P1 million bail – from hearing his malversation case.

The anti-graft court’s Third Division “denied for lack of merit” Revilla’s motion for reconsideration of the denial of his earlier motion intended to make Associate Justice Karl Miranda inhibit from his case.
Miranda, chairman of the Third Division, previously objected to the court’s majority ruling to grant Revilla P1 million bail for his temporary freedom amid his ongoing trial for malversation.
The case stemmed from allegations that he received kickbacks from a P92.8-million ghost flood control project in Pandi, Bulacan.
Miranda asserted it was “difficult to justify” Revilla’s being granted temporary liberty while his co-accused remain behind bars.

In his motion, Revilla accused Miranda of being biased against his bail petition. In contesting his bail petition, Revilla claimed Miranda relied only on “uncorroborated and bare” testimony of state witness former public works undersecretary Roberto Bernardo. Revilla noted Miranda’s brother had acted as Bernardo’s counsel.

In denying his motion for reconsideration, the Sandiganbayan said the former senator “has not presented any new or additional act, conduct, or circumstance that could be considered as clear and convincing evidence of Justice Miranda’s bias and prejudice that would warrant his recusal from hearing the instant case.”

“Justice Miranda has already shown that his Separate Opinion is based on a thorough analysis of all the evidence presented by the prosecution, and thus, it cannot be simply disregarded as evidence of bias or prejudice,” according to the Third Division’s seven-page resolution.
Third Division members Associate Justices Ronald Moreno and Fritz Bryn Anthony delos Santos concurred with the decision.

articles.title: Formal offer of evidence vs VP submitted early
articles.summary: Prosecutors from the House of Representative have submitted their formal offer of evidence against Vice President Sara Duterte to the Senate impeachment court ahead of the deadline last Friday,…

blocks.text: October 25, 2026 | 12:00am

In this photo uploaded on Facebook on July 10, 2026 shows Vice President Sara Duterte during her visit to Miarayon Central Elementary School for the Balik Eskwela program in Miarayon, Talakag, Bukidnon.
Vice President Sara Duterte via Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — Prosecutors from the House of Representative have submitted their formal offer of evidence against Vice President Sara Duterte to the Senate impeachment court ahead of the deadline last Friday, giving the defense 10 days to respond before hearings resume on Nov. 9.

“We already filed our formal offer of evidence, which, I believe if I’m not mistaken, was filed last Oct. 21. And this is days before the deadline,” House impeachment adviser and trial spokesman Robert Ace Barbers said at the Saturday News Forum at Dapo Restaurant in Quezon City.
“Hopefully, before we resume our impeachment hearings they can already file their comment to our formal offer of evidence,” he added.

The formal offer followed the prosecution’s decision to rest its case on Article II, covering Duterte’s unexplained wealth as reflected in her bank records and statements of assets, liabilities and net worth.
Lead prosecutor Rep. Gerville Luistro said the Senate impeachment court must rule on the admissibility of the evidence before the defense presents its case.

“The impeachment court is bound to rule on the admissibility given the formal offer and the comment filed by the defense. And then after that, we proceed to the defense’s presentation of evidence,” the Batangas second district congresswoman said.

“What will be contested upon the formal offer of evidence is the admissibility of evidence. And that is how the prosecution will conclude its presentation of evidence, by filing its formal offer of evidence,” she added.
Luistro said the prosecution presented what it considered strong evidence against Duterte, including documentary and testimonial evidence.
She said it’s the prerogative of the defense to file a demurrer to evidence to challenge the prosecution’s evidence without presenting its own.
“But the Filipino people were able to witness the evidence presented by the prosecution panel,” Luistro said.
“On the contrary, they (prosecution evidence) are strong, clear, convincing. I do not see the ground for filing a demurrer to evidence,” she added.

Luistro also questioned the contrast between Duterte’s public image and the businesses she and her husband Mans Carpio own, citing financial analyst Alexander Cabrera’s findings that GenCorp Foods Corp., a declared asset operated by the Duterte-Carpio couple, runs at least five Jollibee branches.

“The image always being projected is that the respondent, the Vice President, goes to those fish ball stalls, right? She eats at Jollibee. It turns out they own Jollibee,” Luistro said. They have denied the accusation.

articles.title: ‘Visa-free entry likely caused scam hub resurgence’
articles.summary: The abuse of visa-free entry privileges by some foreigners could have contributed to the apparent resurgence of small-scale scam hubs in parts of the country, according to the Department of Justice.

blocks.text: October 25, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The abuse of visa-free entry privileges by some foreigners could have contributed to the apparent resurgence of small-scale scam hubs in parts of the country, according to the Department of Justice.

Justice Undersecretary Nicholas Felix Ty reported that some of the foreigners, mostly Chinese nationals, apprehended in recent raids on scam hubs, particularly in Zamboanga Sibugay earlier this month, entered the Philippines under a visa-free arrangement.

“We cannot deny that this is a privilege we granted to Chinese tourists and that, to some extent, it has been exploited, contributing to this problem,” Ty said at a media briefing last week, acknowledging that the privilege granted to Chinese tourists may have been exploited and contributed to the problem.
Around 200 foreigners were apprehended during the operations. Ty added that some of the foreigners could have been overstaying.
He also said that Chinese nationals recruited to work in local scam hubs may have been instructed to target fellow Chinese citizens before accepting job offers that brought them to the Philippines.
The Department of Foreign Affairs restored visa-free access for Chinese visitors on Jan. 16, allowing visits of up to 14 days strictly for tourism or business purposes.
The arrangement is subject to review before it expires a year after its implementation.
Asked whether Philippine offshore gaming operators (POGOs) and scam hubs were indeed making a comeback across the country, Ty said it was possible.
However, he maintained that the operations were smaller than those previously uncovered, both in scale and in the number of foreign nationals found in the facilities.

“Remember, before, the composition was very international, mostly Chinese, but there were also many Vietnamese, Indonesians and people from Myanmar, Nepal and Africa. Now, those being found are mostly Chinese,” he said.

articles.title: Meghan distressed over dad’s child abuse images in Philippines
articles.summary: British Prince Harry’s wife Meghan is “deeply distressed” by allegations that her father had possessed images of child abuse, adding that she had blocked contact between him and her…

blocks.text: October 25, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — British Prince Harry’s wife Meghan is “deeply distressed” by allegations that her father had possessed images of child abuse, adding that she had blocked contact between him and her children over previous “troubling and disturbing” allegations.
Reports said Meghan’s half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr., allegedly discovered the images while clearing out their father’s former home in Cebu and reported them to Philippine police.
The father denies the allegations, describing them as “sick lies.”
In comments to the Daily Mail, Markle denied the allegations.

“I’m shocked, I’m hurt and I’m very upset that my son is making these accusations against me?” he was quoted by the Daily Mail as saying. “I could never do what I’m being accused of. It’s the worst thing anyone could accuse me of.”
After the reports, Meghan revealed that in 2018 she had seen a letter sent to London’s Metropolitan Police Service and its Royalty and Specialist Protection unit making similar accusations.
“It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated,” she said in a statement.
However, a source close to the matter told AFP that the Metropolitan Police had not investigated the matter and was not investigating it.
Police probe
Following the allegations, Philippine authorities are investigating the 82-year-old man, according to Justice Undersecretary Nicholas Ty.
“Our Anti-Trafficking and Anti-OSAEC (online sexual abuse and exploitation of children) task force in Cebu is currently investigating the matter,” Ty told Reuters.

Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla also told Reuters Markle Jr. had provided authorities with evidence, including a laptop. He also confirmed that Meghan’s father was believed to have returned to the United States.
Melvin Matibag, director of the National Bureau of Investigation, told AP that the FBI had sought the agency’s assistance in examining the allegations.
The FBI office in Manila had transmitted a letter from Markle Jr. to several Philippine law enforcement agencies, including the NBI’s Anti-Violence Against Women and Children Division.
The letter detailed his alleged discovery of materials that appeared to depict children or minors in sexually explicit or exploitative circumstances, Matibag said.
Markle Jr. indicated that he was prepared to surrender the alleged materials and said in an affidavit that his father was in an assisted living facility in Florida, Matibag added.
The FBI requested that Philippine authorities notify it “once any of the victims are identified,” he said.
In a statement, the FBI said it was “aware of the allegations and will provide support, as appropriate, to the Philippine authorities.”
“We will also investigate any related allegations of federal violations of US law,” it added.
The Metropolitan Police said it was aware of media reports that officers from its Royalty and Specialist Protection Command had been involved in passing on a letter in 2018.
“We are undertaking enquiries internally in an effort to confirm this,” a police spokesperson said.

Meghan said she hoped people would understand that her decision to prevent her father from having contact with her children, Prince Archie, seven, and Princess Lilibet, five, was intended to protect them.

“I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children was for one reason: to protect them,” she said.

“Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children,” she added.
Family estrangement

Harry, the younger son of King Charles III, married Meghan, an American former actress who starred in the television drama “Suits,” at Windsor Castle in May 2018. Her father did not attend the wedding.
Days before the ceremony, Markle said he would not attend because of ill health after admitting that he had posed for staged paparazzi photographs for payment.
The wedding and the subsequent estrangement between father and daughter drew extensive media coverage. Markle had never met his grandchildren.
In December, however, a spokesperson for Meghan said she had been in contact with her father while he was in a hospital in the Philippines after having his left leg amputated.
Markle later returned to the US, where he reportedly lives in a rehabilitation or assisted living facility in Florida.

In 2021, Meghan won a privacy and copyright claim in Britain’s High Court against Daily Mail publisher Associated Newspapers over articles that reproduced parts of a private letter she had written to her father, asking him to stop speaking to the press.
Harry and Meghan stepped back from royal duties in 2020 and moved to California. They later returned to the United Kingdom with their children in August.

articles.title: PCO steps up drive vs fake news
articles.summary: Communications Secretary Lino Cayetano has vowed to strengthen the government’s campaign against fake news and disinformation through closer cooperation with media organizations.

blocks.text: October 25, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Communications Secretary Lino Cayetano has vowed to strengthen the government’s campaign against fake news and disinformation through closer cooperation with media organizations.

“We want the help of traditional media, and we want the help of members of the MPC (Malacañang Press Corps),” Cayetano told reporters on Friday when asked about the Presidential Communications Office’s (PCO) fight against misinformation and disinformation.
He said the PCO would establish a system that allows media organizations to independently verify and publish corrections to false information identified by the government.
“So, we’ll have a system, and I think we’ll strengthen the partnership with the private sector and state media with that,” Cayetano said.
He said legal liability would remain with appropriate agencies such as the Department of Justice and the Department of Information and Communications Technology.
On PCO’s action against disinformation about the super El Niño on social media, Cayetano said the agency’s priority is to disseminate factual information to the public.

In March, the PCO, under Cayetano’s predecessor, Dave Gomez, launched the agency’s “Oplan Fake News” in partnership with major broadsheets, including The STAR, to protect the public from the harmful effects of disinformation.
The PCO has established an anti-fake news desk where citizens can report suspicious content for assessment and possible action by relevant agencies.
“If we think there’s something that we can build on, like we’re doing here, we’re building on the success of the past leadership of my former boss, Sec. Dave,” he said.

Meanwhile, Rep. Patrick Michael Vargas personally went to the office of National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag in Quezon City to file formal complaints and submit digital evidence, in a move aimed at shutting down platforms long engaged in producing and spreading fake news.

“Of course, we have always supported the constitutionally guaranteed freedom of speech. But we cannot, in conscience, allow proliferation of these peddlers of fake news. We have to stand up and let them be held accountable for spreading lies repeatedly,” he said.
“They have abused our social media platforms for continuously spreading lies,” he added.
Vargas issued the warning to operators of malicious accounts and troll networks, emphasizing that he will exhaust all legal remedies to unmask their identities and shut down their operations.

Matibag, for his part, assured the lawmaker of the conduct of thorough investigation to expose the full network of administrators, content creators, and financial backers driving the malicious campaign.

The complaint stems from a coordinated campaign of online disinformation, where Facebook pages posing as legitimate news outlets allegedly circulated fabricated allegations including through Artificial Intelligence-manipulated media to mislead the public.

Vargas presented the NBI Cybercrime Division with forensic evidence, including archived screenshots, URL digital traces, and preliminary identification of individuals and administrators operating behind the flagged pages.

He stressed that filing of criminal charges with the NBI goes beyond defending his personal name and integrity, calling it a crackdown against predatory digital syndicates to protect ordinary citizens.

“This battle is not limited to my interest alone, but for every ordinary citizen who have been victimized by this deceit or fraud. We have to nip this in the bud. They have to know and be reminded that they will always be held accountable under our laws,” Vargas maintained.
The filing comes amid growing calls in Congress for stiffer penalties against organized troll networks and coordinated inauthentic behavior on major social media platforms.

Vargas’ legal team affirmed that additional criminal charges under the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012 and administrative complaints would be filed against identified accomplices as the NBI cybercrime probe unfolds.

articles.title: Ping claims TESDA offered him P5 million allocation fund
articles.summary: Sen. Panfilo Lacson has exposed a possible case of corruption in the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority after he declined an offer of P5-million “allocation fund” from…

blocks.text: October 25, 2026 | 12:00am
Senator Ping Lacson attends the Senate’s plenary session in Pasay City on November 18, 2025
STAR / Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Panfilo Lacson has exposed a possible case of corruption in the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) after he declined an offer of P5-million “allocation fund” from the agency’s proposed 2027 budget.
Speaking over dwIZ yesterday, Lacson vowed to ask the TESDA’s budget sponsor during the plenary debate about the P5 million offer, which was made despite his strong position against pork barrel.

“Perhaps they don’t know me because I really don’t accept lobby money,” Lacson said, recalling a time he rejected an offer of money from a congressman – now deceased – brokering for a franchise applicant.

Lacson said he did not think TESDA’s offer was for scholarship for qualified students, because the staff who reached out to him, whom he identified as “Stephanie,” gave a ballpark figure of the money involved. “It doesn’t make sense if it was for scholarship,” Lacson said.
The senator posted on his X account screenshots of the allocation fund offer, allegedly from TESDA Secretary and Director General Jose Francisco Benitez.

“When TESDA’s proposed 2027 budget comes up for plenary debate, I will seek clarification on the P5-million fund offer made to me through my Senate staff early this week. I declined unequivocally,” Lacson wrote in the tweet.
Lacson said he had considered a sting operation but took pity on “Stephanie” who was only following orders.
It was Lacson who had bared the existence of “allocable” funds in the national budget, such as in the Department of Public Works and Highways, for flood control projects..
In a statement, Benitez denied he had authorized anyone to offer Lacson any allocation.
“We welcome the opportunity to get to the bottom of this matter and fully support efforts to establish the facts,” Benitez said, while thanking Lacson for promptly reporting the alleged anomaly.
Benitez said TESDA routinely communicates with senators during budget season to determine if they have concerns regarding the agency’s programs and budget.
However, he stressed that any improper offer, allocation or solicitation involving TESDA funds, or any unauthorized arrangement involving lawmakers run contrary to the agency’s directives.

“I have ordered an immediate internal investigation to determine the truth, identify those responsible for any unauthorized actions or misrepresentations, and apply appropriate administrative and if warranted, criminal cases,” Benitez said. — Gilbert Bayoran

articles.title: Watch as fire engulfs Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat
articles.summary: Police in the southern German state of Bavaria have detained a 33-year-old German man following the fire.

blocks.text: Adolf Hitler's Alpine mountain retreat, known as the Eagle's Nest, was engulfed in flames on Friday night while police arrested a 33-year-old male suspect.
The residence, called the Kehlsteinhaus, is above the town of Berchtesgaden. It was one of several buildings in the area used by the Nazi dictator and his entourage during World War Two.
Hitler also used the area as a backdrop for propaganda films portraying him as a lover of animals and nature.
Local media reported that site had been "largely destroyed", with the public urged to avoid the area.

articles.title: German national facing trial for alleged attempt to join IS
articles.summary: A 21-year-old suspect is being held in pre-trial detention for allegedly trying to join the "Islamic State" terror group.

image.caption: The public prosecutor general (Generalbundesanwalt beim Bundesgerichtshof) is the federal prosecutor of Germany (File: 2019)Image: Christoph Schmidt/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Germany's prosecutor's office said that a German national has been placed in pre-trial detention for allegedly attempting to join the so-called "Islamic State" terror group, while abroad, German news agency dpa reported.
What is known about the case
The agency cited a spokeswoman for the Federal Prosecutor's Office as saying that an arrest warrant had been executed and that a 21-year-old was extradited to Germany.
The suspect is accused of travelling to Ethiopia from Berlin in January 2025, with the purpose of joining the IS terror group in Somalia.
Prosecutors allege that he never reached Somalia, but instead traveled to Pakistan to join IS, where he was reportedly arrested in February 2025.
The suspect stands accused of attempted membership in a terrorist organization abroad. He is also accused of preparing a serious act of violence endangering the state.
Germany and the so-called "Islamic State"
Islamic extremists have carried out several attacks in Germany over the years. The deadliest was when a truck rammed a Berlin Christmas market in 2016, killing 12 people.
In July a German court sentenced a man and a woman to lengthy prison sentences for enslaving and abusing two Yazidi girls under the so-called "Islamic State" group in Iraq.
The Iraqi couple was convicted of war crimes, genocide and crimes against humanity. They were also convicted of sexually abusing children and aiding and abetting the listed offenses.
The couple, identified as Twana H.S. and Asia R.A., in line with German privacy laws, were most recently living in Germany and were arrested in the southern state of Bavaria in April in 2024.

articles.title: Ukraine’s military says Starlink satellite connection stable after recent restrictions
articles.summary:
Volodymyr Zelenskyy offers thanks to US allies for restoring system key to air defence and ‘frontline logistics’

Ukraine’s military has a “stable connection to Starlink”, the Ukrainian…

blocks.text: Ukraine’s military has a “stable connection to Starlink”, the Ukrainian government has said, 10 days after its ability to use the satellite communications system was suddenly restricted.

The Starlink satellite terminals, which are produced by Elon Musk’s SpaceX but managed by the US government, are a key component of Ukraine’s military operations. Sudden speed restrictions on the terminals, which capped operations at speeds of 160km/h (99mph), led to the failure of several Ukrainian combat missions earlier this month.

The military’s ability to intercept Russian attack drones was hampered and some Ukrainian operations to strike behind enemy frontlines were cancelled. Russia was able to launch ballistic missiles at Ukraine without any advance warning from the US.

The speed restrictions coincided with the announcement by Donald Trump of a US deal to buy Russian diesel, although the US president initially denied that his administration was behind the decision to cut intelligence sharing with Ukraine.
“I don’t know if it was anybody, but it wasn’t me, and I don’t think it was Elon,” Trump said, referring to Musk, SpaceX’s chief executive.

However, the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, appeared to throw suspicion on Musk when he defended Trump last Wednesday. “The president has nothing to do with the decisions that are made by Starlink and Starshield and by Mr Musk,” Rubio said. “That’s a private company. The president doesn’t run that company and can’t direct that company to do anything.”

Musk was quick to blame the limits on Starshield on the Trump administration, writing on X last week that the systems were “owned and controlled by the US government”. “Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately Potus [president of the United States],” he wrote.

blocks.caption: Musk blamed the limits on Starshield on the Trump administration, writing on X that the systems were ‘owned and controlled by the US government’. Photograph: Evan Vucci/Reuters

blocks.text: The US vice-president, JD Vance, backed Musk on Thursday, saying the billionaire “doesn’t want to get in the middle of what is a war between two state actors without the United States government effectively directing him on what to do”.
Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, blamed both parties: “It was a message from [the] American government to limit the speed … And technically, SpaceX did it.”
There were no similar restrictions on Starshield terminals in EU countries and that they applied only to Ukraine, he added. “In other words, this is a planned operation.”
He said the decision would “bring a lot of human losses … of course people would die”.
after newsletter promotion

Announcing the restoration of the system on Saturday in a diplomatic video address on the Telegram app, Zelenskyy expressed his gratitude to his US allies, including Trump and the US state department, for resolving the operational issue: “The most important development for ‌today is that Starlink ‌and Starshield have resumed operations at their pre-restriction speeds. The speeds are now at the ‌level we need.”

The restoration began overnight. “By this morning, the speeds were already sufficient for operational use,” Zelenskyy said. “This is very important and significant for our frontline logistics and for defending Ukraine against jet-powered Shaheds.”
On Thursday, Trump had claimed the service was running again at full speed, but a European official speaking to the Associated Press denied the service was fully functioning.

When asked by reporters whether he would tell Musk to stop “messing around” with Ukraine’s access to Starlink on Friday, the US president said: “I’ve not spoken to him. I might have to … I’ve heard it was fixed. But if it’s not, I’ll speak to him … If there is a problem, I’ll get it straightened out.”
He then described Musk as a “very brilliant” and “very good” person.

articles.title: Vanessa Trump says she is cancer-free six months after revealing diagnosis
articles.summary: The ex-wife of Donald Trump Jr, with whom she shares five children, announced in May that she had been diagnosed with breast cancer.

blocks.text: Vanessa Trump, the former wife of Donald Trump Jr, has announced that she is cancer-free following her breast cancer diagnosis earlier this year.

Trump, 48, who has five children with President Donald Trump's eldest son, shared in a short video on her 19-year-old daughter Kai's Instagram account that her recent tests results "came back clear, so I'm finally cancer-free".

The video, posted on Friday, teases the release of a longer YouTube video to come on Saturday, in which Vanessa and Kai Trump will discuss breast cancer awareness and prevention, Kai wrote in the caption.
Vanessa Trump separated from Trump Jr in 2018 and announced last year that she had begun dating US pro golfer Tiger Woods.
"October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month, a time to raise awareness about early detection, education, and support for those affected by breast cancer," Kai Trump wrote on Instagram.
"I sat down with my mom and Dr. Nicole Saphier to talk about my mom's journey with breast cancer and learn more about prevention and early detection," she continued.
Kai's post received over 20,000 likes and hundreds of comments from people offering support and well wishes, including from American singer and media personality Mary Millben.

In Friday's video, Trump said she was first diagnosed with breast cancer in April. She publicly announced the diagnosis in May, saying in a social media post that she had undergone surgery and was working on a treatment plan with her medical team.

According to the American Cancer Society, the average risk of a woman in the US developing breast cancer is about 1 in 8, or 13%. The disease also accounts for 30% of all new female cancers every year, according to the group.
Surgery cures most breast cancers, but if some disease remains, chemotherapy, radiotherapy and endocrine therapy can reduce the long-term risk.
Treatments have been advancing, including more targeted therapies for early breast cancer, new types of hormonal therapies, and more precise and effective radiotherapy.

articles.title: Ombudsman Remulla to gov't: Outsource visa processing, strip DFA of role
articles.summary: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla has called for the outsourcing of visa processing to a third-party service provider, questioning the Department of Foreign Affairs" (DFA) capacity to screen foreigners…

blocks.text: Published October 24, 2026 10:34pm

Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla has called for the outsourcing of visa processing to a third-party service provider, questioning the Department of Foreign Affairs’ (DFA) capacity to screen foreigners seeking entry into the Philippines.
In his program on DZRH, Remulla said visa issuance was an immigration concern that fell under the Department of Justice (DOJ).
“The point is we want to get a background of the people entering our country. And if the DFA is not capable of doing that, give it to VFS (Visa Facilitation Services),” Remulla said.

He was referring to VFS Global, a private outsourcing and technology services company that assists governments and diplomatic missions with the administrative aspects of visa applications, including collecting application forms, supporting documents and biometric data.

Remulla made the statement in reaction to reports that the DFA is reviewing its policy on visa-free entry for Chinese tourists amid concerns that it may have contributed to the expansion of Philippine offshore gaming operator (POGO) activities.

"The DFA’s problem is that it seems to have forgotten that its primary job is to be diplomats. In this case, they want something else to happen—they want to do business. They used to turn visa issuance in China into a business,” he added.
Remulla also claimed that the DFA generated substantial revenues through travel agencies.
He described visa processing as a clerical task and said the Philippines lacked the capacity to perform it effectively in other countries, making a third-party provider such as VFS a better option.
“The DFA should no longer assume that visa processing automatically falls under its responsibility. We have to take it away from them,” Remulla said.
GMA News Online has reached out to the DFA for comment and will update this story once a response is received.—MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Turkey's new deal on Mediterranean maritime boundaries with Libya is exacerbating issues with Greece and the EU
articles.summary: Turkey and Libya plan to redraw maritime boundaries in the Mediterranean as part of a new economic corridor. This has sparked strong protests from Greece, and has also drawn the European Union into…

image.caption: Turkey seeks to strenghten ties with Libya in a bid to extract gas from the eastern Mediterranean in futureImage: ADEM ALTAN/AFP

blocks.text: On Tuesday, the parliament of Libya unanimously approved a maritime agreement with Turkey to establish a direct maritime economic corridor between the countries.

Turkey had agreed on the corridor with the UN-recognized Government of National Accord in western Libya in 2019. However, the agreement faced opposition from the rival Libyan government in the country's east. Now, though, the eastern parliament has reversed its previous opposition.
The decision, which was welcomed by Turkey's Foreign Ministry, is likely to contribute to tensions with other countries in the eastern Mediterranean — especially Greece .

blocks.caption: Ties between Turkey and Libya have improved through joint projectsImage: DHA

blocks.text: 'Null and void'

The agreement establishes a direct maritime corridor between the southern coast of Turkey and the northern coast of Libya. Large oil and gas deposits have recently been discovered in the region in question — estimates suggest that natural gas reserves worth several hundred billion US dollars may lie beneath the seabed. Turkey and Libya aim to secure their economic rights to these raw materials and are seeking to jointly exploit the resources.

The planned corridor disregards Greek islands such as Crete, Karpathos and Rhodes. Greece's government insists that it possesses a comprehensive exclusive economic zone, or EEZ, around these islands and has already announced its opposition to the accord.

In a post on X, the Foreign Ministry announced that Greece firmly rejects the agreement and has the support of the European Union in doing so. "The European Union has described the Turkish-Libyan memorandum as null and void, stressing that it violates the sovereign rights of third states and is not consistent with the Law of the Sea," the ministry posted.

Similar wording came straight from Brussels. "I raised yesterday's Libyan vote on a maritime MoU with Türkiye and stressed that it infringes upon the sovereign rights of third states," Kaja Kallas, the European Union high representative for foreign affairs and security policy, posted on X.
International maritime law

Whose claims are legitimate in the eastern Mediterranean is the central point of contention. Greece primarily cites the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, or UNCLOS. According to Article 121 of the convention, inhabited islands that "support an economic life of their own” have the same rights to an EEZ as the mainland. This applies to Crete, Rhodes and Lesbos.

Athens cites precedents such as a 2022 ruling by the International Court of Justicethat found that Colombia had violated the sovereign rights of Nicaragua by authorizing fishing activities in the Central American country's EEZ. The ICJ found that when interests overlap a fair demarcation must be reached that takes coastlines, geographical conditions and the implications of a potential boundary into account.

Turkey's government argues that the geography of the Mediterranean plays a special role: If every small Greek island off the coast of Turkey and Cyprus were granted a full EEZ, Turkey would be largely cut off from access to the open sea. This, the government argues, must be given greater consideration when demarcating the boundary.

Unlike Greece, Turkey has never signed UNCLOS. Therefore, it does not agree to have the dispute heard by a UN arbitration tribunal. Moreover, even international experts on the law of the sea disagree on what a "fair division” might look like in this specific case.

blocks.caption: Hifter reversed his position on the deal after opposing it for yearsImage: Abdullah Doma/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: When Turkey pushed for the agreement in 2019, a brutal civil war was still raging in Libya. At that time, Turkey intervened militarily in the west to support the government in Tripoli, thereby repelling the offensive by eastern Libyan General Khalifa Hifter.

Since then, the relationship has changed fundamentally: A successful charm offensive by Turkey's government appears to have led to a political rapprochement with Hifter and his camp. Turkey's government now maintains mutually advantageous relations with both parts of Libya. In addition to the countries' plan to develop energy resources in the Mediterranean together, Turkish construction companies have secured contracts worth billions in recent years for Libya's reconstruction. Furthermore, the Turkish state-owned oil company TPAO and the Libyan National Oil Corporation are already working on joint plans for seismic surveys off of Libya's coast.

Turkey's government has established itself as a new military partner for Hifter's forces, supplying weapons and offering training programs. In doing so, Turkey is pushing back against the influence of Egypt and Russia in eastern Libya and strengthening its role as a geopolitical player in the region.
How Turkey quietly became a power broker in Africa

With the agreement now approved in the regional parliament, eastern Libya also aims to secure its share of the lucrative natural resources. This could give Hifter greater international influence in the future. Disputes in the eastern Mediterranean are likely to escalate further as a result of the agreement — particularly once Turkey and Libya begin extracting oil and gas from the disputed maritime area.

The agreement also jeopardizes a major project that is still in the planning stages: the EastMed pipeline, which is intended to transport natural gas from Israel and Cyprus via Greece, thereby making an important contribution to energy security in the European Union. However, the corridor established by Turkey and Libya cuts across the planned route of the pipeline. Turkey has also argued that projects involving cables or pipelines on its claimed continental shelf require its consent.

In the long term, this could lead to a division of the eastern Mediterranean region into two competing energy and defense blocs: The Turkey-Libya axis might be countered by an EU-supported alliance of Greece, Cyprus, Egypt and Israel.
This article was originally published in German.

articles.title: DOTr: Gov't to retain MRT-3 ownership, fare-setting authority under privatization plan
articles.summary: The Department of Transportation (DOTr) said Saturday that the government will retain ownership of the Metro Rail Transit Line 3 (MRT-3) and the authority to set fares under its proposed…

blocks.text: The Department of Transportation (DOTr) said Saturday that the government will retain ownership of the Metro Rail Transit Line 3 (MRT-3) and the authority to set fares under its proposed privatization plan.

In an interview with Super Radyo dzBB, DOTr Undersecretary Timothy John Batan said the proposed public-private partnership (PPP) would transfer only the railway’s operations and maintenance, along with investments for capacity expansion, to the winning private concessionaire.

“Pag sinasabi po natin na privatization ng MRT-3 ay hindi po natin ibinebenta ito pong asset. Hindi po natin ibinebenta o inililipat ang pagmamay-ari ng MRT-3 sa pribadong sektor, kung sino man po ang mananalo. Mananatili po ang pagmamay-ari ng MRT-3, mananatili po ang pagtatakda ng pasahe, ng service quality requirements, ng performance standards. Ito po ay mananatili sa kamay ng gobyerno,” Batan said.

(When we speak of privatizing MRT-3, we are not selling the asset or transferring its ownership to the private sector, whoever the winning bidder may be. Ownership of MRT-3, along with the authority to set fares, service quality requirements, and performance standards, will remain with the government.)
Batan said the government would also set performance standards for the private concessionaire and impose sanctions or penalties for noncompliance.
He stressed that the primary goal of the proposed privatization was to improve MRT-3 facilities and services, rather than generate revenue for the government.
“Ang pangunahing benepisyo po natin na… nilalayong makita dito sa proyekto na ito ay hindi po pinansyal. Hindi po tayo pumapasok sa proyekto na ito para po kumita ang gobyerno,” Batan said.
(The main benefit we aim to achieve through this project is not financial. We are not undertaking this project to generate profits for the government.)

“Pangunahin po nating layunin na maibigay ‘yung mataas na kalidad po ng serbisyo doon po sa ating mananakay. ‘Yan pong mataas na kalidad na serbisyo na ’yan ay una sa lahat, manggagaling sa capacity expansion,” he added.
(Our primary goal is to provide high-quality service to commuters. This will primarily be achieved through capacity expansion.)
The DOTr said the revenue-sharing arrangements for MRT-3 were still under review and undergoing approval by the Investment Coordination Committee and the Economic Development Council.
Batan, however, said the proposed arrangement would have fare revenues go directly to the government.

The agency assured commuters that the government would retain control over fares to keep them affordable, saying service improvements would be of little use if passengers could not afford to ride the trains.
Capacity expansion

MRT-3 currently has a daily passenger capacity of 500,000, with trains operating in three-car configurations and a signaling system that allows intervals of about three and a half minutes between trains.
Under the proposed PPP, the DOTr aims to increase the line’s daily capacity to as many as one million passengers and reduce train intervals to two minutes.

Batan said technical studies were ongoing with the Asian Development Bank (ADB), the agency’s adviser, to determine whether MRT-3’s capacity could be increased to 800,000, 900,000, or even one million passengers daily.

“Ongoing po ‘yung teknikal na pag-aaral, kasama po ng ating adviser galing sa Asian Development Bank (ADB), kung ito pong kapasidad na nasa 500,000 a day ay maiaakyat po natin to 800,000 to 900,000 or even one million passengers a day,” he said.

(A technical study is underway with our adviser from the Asian Development Bank to determine whether the current capacity of 500,000 passengers a day can be increased to 800,000, 900,000, or even one million.)

Batan said the expansion would involve acquiring additional train cars to convert all trains to four-car configurations and upgrading the signaling system to reduce train intervals from three and a half minutes to two minutes.
The DOTr acknowledged that overcrowding at stations during peak hours underscored the need to replace aging train cars, upgrade signaling equipment, and reduce passenger waiting times.
Batan said tapping the private sector would allow the government to benefit from experienced railway operators and secure additional capital for the necessary investments.
The DOTr said it was finalizing the concession structure, in coordination with the ADB, including arrangements for recovering private investments.
Timeline
Batan said the current maintenance partnership between the government and Sumitomo Corporation for MRT-3 would end in December 2027.
Under the proposed PPP, operations and maintenance would be consolidated under a single private operator to establish a single point of responsibility.
The DOTr aims to finalize the PPP terms and secure the necessary approvals by December 2026, before proceeding with an open, solicited bidding process for prospective concessionaires.
The agency targets awarding the MRT-3 PPP concession contract by the third quarter of 2027. — VBL, GMA News
